The economics are absurd and the workshop says so. Metal type costs four times what it did in 1990, the sole foundry capable of casting it is located abroad, and the press's engineer is sixty-eight and has no apprentice. Last year's edition ran at a substantial loss, which the society covered from a charitable legacy.

The argument for continuing is not economic and the society's chair does not pretend otherwise. He says the workshop is the only place in the country where a pupil can see how a page was made before computers, and that four schools sent classes last year, which is four more than in 2019.

The apprentice question is the one nobody can answer, and it is now urgent: a charitable foundation has offered a grant on condition that the workshop takes on a paid trainee, and the society has not yet replied. The engineer has trained two people in twenty years and both left for jobs in design, and he says the work is not difficult, only slow, and that slowness is precisely what nobody will pay for.

questions.stem: What does the workshop produce each year?
options: A single collection of local records.
questions.answer: A single collection of local records.
questions.explanation: 首段与第二段都说明每年只印一本书，内容是本地档案汇编，为两百名会员而印。C 项说印字体样本册、B 项说为四所学校印教材、A 项说重印十九世纪小说，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why do members pay for the hand-printed copies?
options: Because they are cheaper than modern reprints.
Because of how they were made rather than what they contain.
Because the society forbids other editions.
Because the paper is stronger than modern paper.
questions.answer: Because of how they were made rather than what they contain.
questions.explanation: 原文说会员买的是“知道这一百五十册是按初版的方式做出来的”，即制作方式本身。A 项说比现代重印便宜，原文说现代版只要三分之一价钱；C 项说协会禁止其他版本，原文说多数人两种都买；D 项说纸张更结实，原文只提晾纸一周。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：付费动机的实质

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To explain how paper is dried.
To set out the financial difficulty without softening it.
To compare two kinds of metal type.
questions.answer: To set out the financial difficulty without softening it.
questions.explanation: 该段先承认经济上荒谬，随后列出字体涨价四倍、铸造厂在外国、工程师无人接班、去年亏损，功能是把财务困境如实摆出。D 项比较字体、A 项讲晾纸、C 项讲工程师培训，都不是该段主体，其中 C 项属末段。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：问题段的构成
and the workshop says so 的态度

questions.stem: What does the society's chair argue?
options: That the engineer should retire immediately.
That the society should raise its membership fee.
That the workshop shows pupils something a printed book cannot.
That the press should be replaced by a modern machine.
questions.answer: That the workshop shows pupils something a printed book cannot.
questions.explanation: 会长说这是全国唯一能让小学生看到“电脑之前一页纸如何做出”的地方，并用四所学校来访佐证，重点在教育价值而非经济。B 项说应提高会费、D 项说应换新机器、A 项说工程师应立即退休，原文都没有，其中 D 项与全篇立场相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：论证重心的转移

passages.passage:
A firm of architects asked its staff to estimate how long a project would take and, when it was finished, to record how long it had actually taken. The comparison, published last year, is a catalogue of optimism: the average estimate was forty per cent below the truth, and not one of the ninety projects finished early.

The pattern is familiar to psychologists, who call it the planning fallacy, and it survives information. Architects who had been wrong on their last project were wrong on the next one by almost exactly the same amount, which suggests that the error is not a failure of memory but a feature of how a plan is imagined, and that teaching people about the fallacy has almost no effect on the figures they produce.

What the firm found useful was not the size of the error but its shape. Estimates were closest to reality for small projects with a single client and furthest for large ones with a committee, and the difference was almost entirely explained by the number of people whose approval a stage required. A committee does not add work; it adds waiting, and waiting is what nobody puts in a plan.

The firm did not respond by demanding longer estimates. It asked for two numbers instead of one, the date by which a project would probably finish and the date by which it would almost certainly finish, and it now shows both to the client. The second number is the one the firm plans against, and the first is the one it hopes for.

Whether this has improved anything is unclear. Two years of figures show that projects still run late against the probable date, though less late than before, and the partner who introduced the change says he would rather be honest and late than confident and later.

The psychologists' warning is worth repeating. Estimating is not a skill that improves reliably with feedback, and a firm that expects its staff to get better at it through experience is expecting something the evidence does not support. The firm has stopped using the exercise as training and uses it instead as a warning.

questions.stem: How far off were the architects' estimates on average?
options: Forty per cent longer than the real time.
Forty per cent short of the real time.
questions.answer: Forty per cent short of the real time.
questions.explanation: 原文说平均估计比实际低百分之四十，即估短了四成。B 项方向相反；C 项说只差一成，数字不符；A 项说几乎准确，与“九十项没有一个提前完成”矛盾。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：百分比与方向

questions.stem: What is the planning fallacy?
options: A refusal to make any estimate at all.
A belief that committees work faster.
A systematic underestimate that experience does not correct.
A habit of finishing projects early.
questions.answer: A systematic underestimate that experience does not correct.
questions.explanation: 原文把它定义为一种普遍低估，并且“经得起信息冲击”：上次估错的人下次照样估错同样的量。A 项说拒绝估算、D 项说习惯提前完工（与“无一项提前”相反）、B 项说相信委员会更快（原文说委员会增加等待），都不成立。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To explain what made the error larger or smaller.
To list the firm's completed projects.
To argue that estimates should be longer.
questions.answer: To explain what made the error larger or smaller.
questions.explanation: 该段把注意力从误差大小转到误差形状：单人客户的小项目估得准，有委员会的大项目估得最不准，原因是审批环节带来等待。C 项列举项目、B 项比较两类人、D 项主张延长估算（原文恰说没有那样做），都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：从现象到成因

questions.stem: Why does the firm show clients two dates?
options: Because the probable date is unreliable.
Because clients demanded a shorter schedule.
So they can see the gap between hope and likelihood.
So the firm can charge twice for planning.
questions.answer: So they can see the gap between hope and likelihood.
questions.explanation: 两个日期分别是“可能完成”和“几乎必然完成”，公布两者就是让客户看到希望与概率之间的差距，并以较保守的一个安排工作。D 项说借此重复收费、B 项说客户要求缩短工期、A 项说可能日期不可靠，都与原文逻辑相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：两个数字的功能

passages.passage:
A hotel in the centre of the city stopped issuing cleaning routes last year and asked its thirty cleaners to design their own, and the general manager says rooms are now cleaned in twenty minutes less time than before.

The old routes had been designed by a consultancy in 2015, with a stopwatch and a clipboard, and they were efficient on paper: each cleaner was assigned a floor, and the floor was cleaned from the top down in a fixed sequence. That sequence was timed at eleven minutes a room, which the consultancy called a benchmark and the cleaners called a fantasy.

The cleaners' objection, which the consultancy recorded and the hotel ignored, was that the plan assumed an empty corridor. In practice a trolley blocks the passage, a guest leaves late, a lift is under repair, and the fixed sequence turns a short obstruction into a long one, because a cleaner who has to return to the top of the floor loses the time twice.

The new arrangement has no fixed sequence at all. Each cleaner is told which rooms must be ready by eleven and which can wait until two, and the route between them is her own, decided on the floor rather than in an office. The hotel has kept the stopwatch; it has stopped using it to score anybody.

The saving is real and it is not the interesting part. What the manager reports with greater surprise is that complaints about rooms cleaned late fell by two thirds in the first quarter, and that four cleaners who had been on long-term sick leave came back to work.

The manager is careful about the claim. He says the change would not have worked without the two-hour window, that some hotels cannot offer one because their guests depart at different times, and that a cleaner who designs a poor route has only herself to blame, which is a fairer arrangement than it sounds and a considerably harder one to manage. He has been invited to explain it at a conference of hotel managers in the autumn and has not decided whether to accept.

questions.stem: What did the hotel stop doing last year?
options: Giving each cleaner a fixed route.
Asking guests to leave by eleven.
questions.answer: Giving each cleaner a fixed route.
questions.explanation: 首段说饭店不再下发固定清洁路线，改由清洁工自定。D 项说不再雇三十人，人数未变；B 项说完全不用秒表，原文说仍保留但不再用来评分；C 项说要求客人十一点前离开，原文只提到房间何时必须备好。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：停止行为的界定

questions.stem: Why was the fixed sequence inefficient in practice?
options: Cleaners refused to follow it at all.
The floors were too large to finish.
The stopwatch measured the wrong task.
Any interruption made a cleaner lose time twice.
questions.answer: Any interruption made a cleaner lose time twice.
questions.explanation: 原文说固定顺序一旦被打断，清洁工要回到楼层顶端，等于把损失的时间赔两遍。A 项说清洁工完全不听，原文说问题在方案假设空走廊而非抗拒；B 项说楼层太大、C 项说秒表测错任务，都不是原文给出的原因。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：因果链的还原
loses the time twice 的含义

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To report a benefit the manager had not expected.
To explain how trolleys are stored.
questions.answer: To report a benefit the manager had not expected.
questions.explanation: 该段一开始就点明“节省不是有趣的部分”，随后报出投诉下降三分之二、四名长期病假者返岗这两项意外收获，功能是呈现未预期的效果。C 项比较两家清洁公司、D 项讲推车存放、A 项批评清洁工路线，都不是该段内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：转折句后的新信息

questions.stem: What does "window" mean in the last paragraph?
options: The time a guest spends checking in.
A glass opening in the hotel wall.
A gap in the lift's schedule.
The time allowed for the morning's rooms to be finished.
questions.answer: The time allowed for the morning's rooms to be finished.
questions.explanation: 上文说房间分两批备好（十一点与两点），因此“两小时窗口”指允许清洁先后安排的时段。B 项指墙上的窗，属字面义；C 项指电梯时刻的空档、A 项指办理入住的时间，都与“没有它这套办法就不成立”不匹配。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 词义猜测：抽象名词的语境义

passages.passage:
A reservoir that supplies a city of half a million people is drawn down every spring, deliberately, to a level that looks alarming in photographs, and the water is released slowly through the summer to keep a town downstream from flooding.

The rule behind this was written after 2007, when the reservoir filled in March and the town below it flooded in June. The engineers who wrote it did not try to hold more water; they accepted that a full reservoir in spring is a reservoir with no room for rain, and they set a target level for the first of April lower than the one their predecessors had defended for thirty years.

The cost is paid upstream and it is visible. Marinas lose their moorings, a sailing club has moved twice, and the shoreline in April is a hundred metres of mud that the tourist office would rather nobody photographed. The benefit is paid downstream and it is invisible, because a flood that does not happen leaves no trace and no photograph, and nobody thanks an engineer for a dry street, which is the whole of the difficulty.

The economics are unequal in a way the engineers acknowledge. The city receives its water, the town receives its protection, and the people who lose are those who own boats and run cafés beside the water. A compensation scheme exists and pays out about eleven thousand pounds a year, which is a fraction of what the marinas say they lose.

What has changed since 2007 is the size of the drawdown. It has been increased twice, in 2015 and again in 2022, because rainfall in the catchment has become less reliable rather than smaller, and a reservoir that depends on steady rain needs more empty space when the rain arrives in sudden bursts.

The engineer who wrote the original rule is now retired and says he would write it again. He also says the argument he won in 2007 would be harder to win today, because the people who pay for it have learned to photograph the mud and the people who benefit have never had to explain themselves.

questions.stem: Why is the reservoir drawn down every spring?
options: To leave space for rain and limit flooding downstream.
To allow engineers to inspect the dam.
To supply the city's marinas with water.
To make the shoreline easier to photograph.
questions.answer: To leave space for rain and limit flooding downstream.
questions.explanation: 原文说工程师的逻辑是“春天装满的水库没有余地接雨”，因此刻意降低水位以削峰。C 项说为游艇码头供水、B 项说便于检查大坝、D 项说便于拍照，都不是原文给出的理由，其中 D 项恰是被抱怨的现象。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: no room for rain 的含义

questions.stem: Why is the downstream benefit described as invisible?
options: Because the town is too far away to photograph.
Because the engineers keep their records secret.
Because the water is released at night.
Because a flood that never happens leaves nothing to see.
questions.answer: Because a flood that never happens leaves nothing to see.
questions.explanation: 原文把“没有发生的洪水”与“没有痕迹、没有照片”并列，说明收益之所以看不见，是因为它以“未发生的事件”形式存在。A 项说城镇太远、B 项说记录保密、C 项说夜间放水，原文都没有；C 项尤其没有任何依据。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：以“未发生”形式存在的收益

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To compare two cities' water use.
To list the marina owners' complaints.
To explain why the drawdown has grown since 2007.
questions.answer: To explain why the drawdown has grown since 2007.
questions.explanation: 该段先说“变化的是降水的幅度”，再解释原因：降雨变得不可靠而非变少，靠稳定降雨的水库需要更大的空余容量。D 项讲大坝修建、A 项比较两城用水、B 项列举码头主抱怨（那属第三段），都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：解释变化原因
less reliable rather than smaller 的辨析

questions.stem: What does the retired engineer imply about winning the argument today?
options: That the rainfall data has become unreliable.
That visible losers now outweigh invisible beneficiaries.
That engineers no longer write such rules.
That the town has stopped flooding entirely.
questions.answer: That visible losers now outweigh invisible beneficiaries.
questions.explanation: 他说“付代价的人学会了拍泥滩，受益的人从来不必为自己辩解”，暗示今天的舆论天平偏向可见的受损者。A 项说降雨数据变得不可靠，那是客观变化而非他的言外之意；D 项说城镇已完全不再受淹，原文未提；C 项说工程界不再制定此类规则，也无依据。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：对比句的暗示
可见与不可见的政治分量

passages.passage:
The city's marathon abolished its four-hour cut-off in 2023, and the number of runners finishing between four and six hours has since doubled, while the number finishing under three hours has not moved at all.

The cut-off had existed for reasons that were entirely practical. A marathon is run on streets that belong to somebody else for the rest of the day, and the police would only grant a licence on condition that every road was reopened by two in the afternoon. Four hours was not a judgement about ability; it was the latest start that made the licence workable, and it had been chosen by an engineer with a stopwatch rather than by anybody with a view about runners.

What changed the calculation was a collapse in 2019. A runner went down at the twenty-fourth mile, four hours and twenty minutes into the race, at a point where the marshals had already been stood down and the water stations had been packed away, and it took eleven minutes for anybody with medical training to reach him. He survived, and the inquiry that followed asked a question the organisers could not answer: what exactly was the cut-off protecting?

The answer, once it was written down, turned out to be the licence and nothing else. The medical cover had been organised around the cut-off rather than the other way round, and it was cheaper that way. The 2023 race therefore reopened the roads in stages, behind a sweep bus that follows the last runner, and doubled the medical cover along the final six miles; the entry fee rose by six pounds to pay for it.

The runners who gained most are the ones the sport usually ignores: first-timers, runners over sixty, and the several hundred who run for charities and need five and a half hours to do it. The runners who lost something are the fast ones, who now share the first three miles with a much larger field and find the start slower than it was.

The race director is honest about that. He says a marathon is a race for one afternoon and a street for the remainder of the day, and that a city which closes its streets for six hours is making a claim about who the streets are for. He also says he would not have won the argument in 2019, and that the collapse is what won it for him.

questions.stem: What did the marathon abolish in 2023?
options: Its medical cover along the last six miles.
questions.explanation: 首段明确说取消四小时关门时限，随后给出四到六小时完赛人数翻倍的结果。A 项说取消慈善名额、C 项说取消最后六英里的医疗覆盖（原文是加倍）、B 项说取消分段解封（原文是改成分段解封），三项都与原文相反。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why did the organisers keep a cut-off before 2023?
options: It reduced the cost of medical cover to nothing.
It was the latest finish that let them reopen the roads on time.
It kept slower runners from entering the race.
It was required by the runners' association.
questions.answer: It was the latest finish that let them reopen the roads on time.
questions.explanation: 原文说四小时与能力判断无关，只是让道路两点前解封、使执照成立的最晚起算点。C 项说为挡住慢跑者，原文明确否认这是能力判断；A 项说把医疗成本降为零，原文只说更便宜；D 项说跑步协会要求，原文未提。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：制度性原因的识别
not a judgement about ability 的排除作用

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To explain how a runner collapsed in 2019.
To show how the safety objection was answered in practice.
To describe the route of the 2023 race.
To compare entry fees across years.
questions.answer: To show how the safety objection was answered in practice.
questions.explanation: 该段先指出医疗覆盖原本是围着关门时间安排的，再交代 2023 年的三项具体改动（分段解封、收尾巴士、医疗加倍）与费用上涨，功能是把安全质疑落到可执行的安排上。C 项描述赛道、D 项比较报名费（只提涨了六镑）、A 项讲 2019 年那次倒下（属第三段），都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：从质疑到方案的落地

questions.stem: Why does the passage mention the faster runners' complaint?
options: To admit a cost the change imposed on one group.
To suggest the change should be reversed.
To argue that fast runners should be seeded separately.
To show that the field has become too large to manage.
questions.answer: To admit a cost the change imposed on one group.
questions.explanation: 原文并列写出“获益最大的人”与“失去了一些东西的人”，并借赛事总监之口承认这一点，目的是不掩饰改革对某一群体的代价。C 项主张分段起跑、D 项说参赛规模失控、B 项建议撤回改革，原文都没有，其中 B 项与末段“不会退回 2019 年”相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 写作意图：主动呈现反面成本

passages.passage:
A museum in the west of the country agreed last year to return a bronze head to the country it came from, and the negotiations took four years, which is quick by the standards of such cases.

The head had been in the collection since 1897, acquired from a soldier's estate with a bill of sale that was, in the words of the museum's own catalogue, of doubtful validity. Nobody had disputed the entry for a century, partly because nobody had asked; the request came from a regional museum that had been assembling the pieces of a single figure for thirty years and had already recovered three of them.

What made the case unusual was the museum's decision to publish its correspondence. Every letter, including the ones in which its own lawyers advised that it could probably keep the head, was placed online with the agreement of both parties, and the effect was to move the argument from the outcome to the reasoning.

The reasoning was not flattering. The lawyers were right: the bill of sale had been defective, but the law that governed it had been repealed in 1963, and no court would have ordered restitution. The museum returned the head because it decided that a defective title obtained in a colonial war was not the kind of title it wished to hold, which is a moral argument and not a legal one.

The plinth where the head had stood is now empty, and the museum has not filled it. A label explains that the object is on loan, indefinitely, to the museum that asked for it, and that the loan may be renewed but cannot be sold; beside it is a photograph of the figure as it would look whole, with four pieces in place and the fifth marked in outline.

The director has been criticised for both halves of that arrangement. Some visitors say an empty plinth is an admission that the collection was built on theft; others say a label is a cheap substitute for an object and that the museum has kept the photograph and given away the thing itself.

Her answer is that a museum is a place where objects are explained, and that an explanation is not improved by pretending the object's history began when it arrived. She adds that she has been asked to advise three other institutions and has told all three the same thing: publish the correspondence first, because a decision that cannot be argued with will not be believed.

questions.stem: What did the museum decide to do with the bronze head?
options: Lend it to a private collector for a fee.
Sell it to recover the cost of four years of talks.
Return it to the museum that had requested it.
Keep it and publish an apology.
questions.answer: Return it to the museum that had requested it.
questions.explanation: 首段说博物馆同意归还铜头像，末段又说该物件以无限期借展方式交给索求的博物馆。B 项说出售、D 项说保留并致歉、A 项说有偿借给私人收藏者，原文都没有，其中 B 项与“cannot be sold”直接冲突。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：处置方式的界定

questions.stem: What is the passage's main point about ownership claims?
options: They become stronger each year an object is held.
They are always decided by the courts that hear them.
They should be left to the countries that lost the objects.
They can be settled without settling what an object means.
questions.answer: They can be settled without settling what an object means.
questions.explanation: 全文的转折点是：法律上博物馆本可保留，它却因道德理由归还，并强调解释并不因物件的去留而完成，即归属可以了结而意义不能。B 项说总由法院裁决，与“没有法院会判归还”相反；A 项说持有越久主张越强，原文未提；C 项把主张完全交给来源国，过于绝对。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 主旨理解：法律与道德的分离

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To compare two national museums' collections.
To show what the museum did with the space left behind.
To describe how bronze heads were cast.
questions.answer: To show what the museum did with the space left behind.
questions.explanation: 该段写空着的基座、说明牌、借展条件与那张“补齐四件、第五件勾出轮廓”的照片，功能是交代物件离开后原址如何处置。C 项讲铸造工艺、A 项比较两家馆藏、D 项列举投诉（属末段），都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：空位处理的信息设计
indefinitely 与 cannot be sold 的作用

questions.stem: Why did the museum publish all of its correspondence?
options: So the sale could be completed more quickly.
So the other museum would drop its request.
So the decision could be judged on its reasons rather than its result.
So the lawyers could be protected from criticism.
questions.answer: So the decision could be judged on its reasons rather than its result.
questions.explanation: 原文说公开往来信函的效果是把争论从“结果”移到“理由”，末段又说“不能与之辩驳的决定不会被相信”，可见目的在于让公众按理由评判。D 项说保护律师、B 项说让对方撤回请求、A 项说加快成交，原文都无依据，其中 A 项与“并未出售”相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: outcome 与 reasoning 的对照

passages.passage:
A hospital in the south of the city employs four interpreters, and the one who has been there longest says her job is not to translate words but to translate expectations, which is a different and harder task.

The words are the easy part. A patient who says she has a headache means something narrower than a doctor hears, and an interpreter who renders it faithfully has done her job and failed her patient; the interpreters are therefore trained to say what a phrase probably means in the language of the clinic and to flag it when they are guessing.

The doctors were suspicious of this for years. Several said they wanted the patient's words and not the interpreter's opinion, and one consultant wrote a letter arguing that an interpreter who edits is an interpreter who has decided what the patient is allowed to say. The hospital's response was to record a sample of consultations, with everyone's consent, and to play them back to the clinicians who had complained.

The recording that changed the argument runs for eleven minutes. A woman describes a pain in her chest, the interpreter asks her a question in her own language, the woman answers at length, and the interpreter tells the doctor: she thinks it is the same pain as last year, when her brother died, and she is afraid of the ward. The doctor's note, written afterwards, says chest pain, no cardiac history; the interpreter's note says the same thing and adds the fear.

Nobody is claiming that the interpreters are always right. They work in three languages and the hospital serves speakers of nine, they are not clinicians, and the longest-serving one says she has been wrong in ways that frightened her. What she argues is narrower: a translation that removes the patient's uncertainty about what is being asked is not more accurate, only more literal.

The hospital has since changed the contract. Interpreters now sit in on the first appointment and the discharge conversation rather than being called when a doctor decides one is needed, and the budget line has doubled. The figure the finance office quotes in defence of the change is not a saving but a reduction: readmissions within a month fell by a fifth in the first year, which is the sort of number that ends arguments in a hospital.

questions.stem: What does the longest-serving interpreter say her job is?
options: To convey what patients mean, not only what they say.
To teach doctors a third language.
To write the discharge notes for the doctors.
To decide which patients are seen first.
questions.answer: To convey what patients mean, not only what they say.
questions.explanation: 原文说她译的不是词而是期待，即把病人的表述按其真实含义转给医生。B 项说教医生外语、C 项说代写出院记录、D 项说决定就诊顺序，原文都没有；C 项虽有 note 出现，但说话人是医生与口译各自记，不是代写。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：岗位职责的界定

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To show why the interpreters' approach prevailed.
To explain how recordings are stored.
To summarise a patient's medical history.
questions.answer: To show why the interpreters' approach prevailed.
questions.explanation: 该段完整还原那段十一分钟的录音，并对比医生记录与口译记录，用具体证据说明为何反对意见被说服。D 项只是复述病历、B 项批评医生记录（原文只作对照未作评价）、C 项讲录音如何保存，都不是该段用意。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：以证据改变争论

questions.stem: What is the passage's central claim about interpreting?
options: Recording consultations should be standard practice.
Doctors should learn the languages their patients speak.
Interpreters should never add information to what is said.
A literal rendering can be less accurate than an interpretive one.
questions.answer: A literal rendering can be less accurate than an interpretive one.
questions.explanation: 末段借口译之口给出核心主张：抹掉病人对“在问什么”的不确定，不是更准确，只是更字面。C 项说绝不可增补信息，正是全文要反驳的观点；B 项主张医生学外语、A 项主张录音常规化，都只是文中的手段或细节。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 主旨理解：准确与字面的区分

questions.stem: What does "a reduction" refer to in the last paragraph?
options: A cut in the hospital's interpreter budget.
A decrease in the number of languages served.
A shorter average length of a consultation.
A fall in the number of patients readmitted soon after leaving.
questions.answer: A fall in the number of patients readmitted soon after leaving.
questions.explanation: 原文说这个“减少”指一个月内再入院人数下降五分之一，财务处正用它为增加预算辩护。A 项说削减口译预算（原文是翻倍）；C 项说问诊时长变短、B 项说服务语种减少，都与 readmissions fell 无关。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 词义猜测：抽象名词的所指
not a saving but a reduction 的转折

passages.passage:
The town's weekly paper closed in 2018 after ninety-four years, and the question that the closure left behind was not whether the town would miss it but what would do its work.

Three things arrived in the gap. A Facebook group, started by a retired teacher, now has eleven thousand members and carries more local news than the paper ever did; a regional news site covers the town from an office thirty miles away, with one reporter and a shared photographer; and the council began publishing its own minutes, in full, for the first time.

The group is the one that people praise. It is fast, it is free, and it caught a planning dispute that the regional site missed entirely. It is also, by the retired teacher's own account, unreliable in a way that a newspaper was not: nobody checks a claim before posting it, the same photograph circulates with three different captions, and the most energetic contributors are the ones with a grievance.

The regional site is accurate and thin. Its reporter covers four towns, files two stories a week about this one, and has never been to a council meeting in person; the paper's former editor says the site is what the paper would have been if it had sacked everybody except the sub-editor.

The council's minutes are the strangest of the three. They are complete, they are free, and almost nobody reads them, because a minute is a record of a decision and not an account of an argument. The former editor, who now reads them every week, says the paper's real product was never the news but the sense that somebody was in the room; a minute proves that a decision was taken and cannot show who was persuaded.

What has not been replaced at all is the court report. The paper sent a trainee to the magistrates' court every Thursday for forty years, and the group has never sent anybody, so the fines imposed on local landlords and shoplifters now go unrecorded except in a register that nobody consults.

The retired teacher is careful about the word substitute. She says the group does something the paper could not, and that it cannot do what the paper did, and that a town which had one of those things for ninety-four years has not yet worked out what it needs.

questions.stem: What happened to the town's weekly paper in 2018?
options: It was taken over by the council.
It moved to a regional office thirty miles away.
questions.explanation: 首段明确说周报在 2018 年停刊，已经办了九十四年。D 项说搬到三十英里外的地区办公室，那是新出现的地区新闻站；A 项说被市政厅接管（原文是市政厅开始自行公布会议纪要）；C 项说变成脸书群组，那是退休教师另建的。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：主体与事件的对应

questions.stem: What is the weakness of the Facebook group?
options: Nothing is checked before it is posted.
It charges members for local news.
It is slower than the regional site.
It refuses to cover planning disputes.
questions.answer: Nothing is checked before it is posted.
questions.explanation: 原文说群里发帖前无人核实、同一张照片配三种说明，可见弱点是缺少核查。B 项说向成员收费（原文是 free）；C 项说比地区网站慢（原文说它 fast）；D 项说拒报规划争议（原文说它恰恰抓到了规划争议）。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：由例证归纳缺陷
the same photograph 的细节作用

questions.stem: What is the main function of the sixth paragraph?
options: To identify something the town has lost without replacement.
To describe how magistrates' courts work.
To argue that fines should be higher.
To compare two local newspapers' circulations.
questions.answer: To identify something the town has lost without replacement.
questions.explanation: 该段以“完全没有被替代的是什么”开头，只讲法院庭审报道这一项，并说明四十年间由实习生每周四采写、如今无人接手，功能是指出独一份的空白。B 项讲法院运作、D 项比较两家发行量、C 项主张提高罚金，都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：以“未被替代”定位缺口

questions.stem: What does the passage suggest a minute cannot do?
options: Show who was persuaded and why.
Record that a decision was taken.
Be read by anybody at all.
questions.answer: Show who was persuaded and why.
questions.explanation: 前主编的原话是：纪要能证明决定已作出，却无法显示谁被说服，即缺的是过程与理由。B 项说记录决定已作出，那恰是纪要能做到的；C 项说无人阅读（原文是 almost nobody，且属另一判断）；D 项说未经表决即可公布，原文未提。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：纪要与报道的分工
somebody was in the room 的含义

passages.passage:
The bus that ran twice a day between the village and the market town stopped in 2021, and what replaced it is not a bus: eight residents now share two cars, and a booking sheet pinned up in the shop decides who travels when.

The bus had carried an average of four passengers a trip, and the council's subsidy worked out at eleven pounds a head; the operator withdrew the route when the subsidy was cut and no company bid to take it on. The parish council's first proposal was to fight for the subsidy, and its second, which was adopted after a single meeting, was to buy a second-hand car and insure eight drivers.

The scheme is not a taxi service and the residents are careful to say so. Journeys must be booked a day ahead, they must begin or end in the village, and a driver may refuse a request if the trip clashes with a hospital appointment or a school run; the rules run to two pages and were argued over for longer than the car took to buy.

What has surprised the organisers is who uses it. They expected the scheme to serve people without cars, and it does, but half the journeys are made by people who own a car and would rather not take it into town on a Saturday because of the parking. The car is therefore doing two jobs, and the booking sheet is the only place where both are visible.

The economics are fragile and nobody pretends otherwise. Insurance for eight named drivers costs more than the subsidy ever did, the car will need replacing in about four years, and the scheme depends on a volunteer who keeps the sheet and another who keeps the accounts. A second car was added last year and the volunteer says the sheet is now the busiest thing in the village.

The council has cited the scheme in a report on rural transport, and the report is careful in a way that the residents are not: it notes that eight drivers and two cars can serve a village of four hundred people and cannot serve a valley of four thousand, and that what has been replaced is not a bus but the assumption that a bus is the only answer.

questions.stem: What replaced the bus in 2021?
options: Two cars shared by eight local drivers.
questions.answer: Two cars shared by eight local drivers.
questions.explanation: 首段说八个村民共用两辆车，并用店里的预约表安排出行。A 项说是议会补贴的小巴（原文说补贴被削减）、C 项说是商业出租公司（原文说无人投标）、D 项说是赶集日大巴，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：替代方案的具体形态

questions.stem: Why did the bus route end?
options: The council banned buses from the village.
Too few residents owned cars to use it.
Funding was withdrawn and no firm tendered for the route.
The road became too narrow for a bus.
questions.answer: Funding was withdrawn and no firm tendered for the route.
questions.explanation: 原文把停运直接连到“补贴被削减”与“无公司投标”两件事。B 项说村民拥有汽车太少（原文说半数行程来自有车者）；A 项说议会禁行巴士、D 项说道路太窄，原文均无依据。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：两条并列原因
withdraw 与 bid 的因果

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To compare two models of car.
To correct an assumption about who the users are.
To list the scheme's insurance costs.
questions.answer: To correct an assumption about who the users are.
questions.explanation: 该段以“令人意外的是使用者是谁”开头，指出半数行程来自本已有车、只是不愿进城找车位的人，功能是修正“只服务无车者”的预设。C 项列举保险成本（属下一段）、D 项描写村中小店、A 项比较车型，都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：以“意外”纠正常见预设
half the journeys 的证据作用

questions.stem: What does the council's report emphasise?
options: That the scheme suits a small village, not a whole valley.
That the second car was a mistake.
That the volunteers should be paid a salary.
That the scheme should be extended to every village.
questions.answer: That the scheme suits a small village, not a whole valley.
questions.explanation: 原文说报告措辞比村民谨慎：八名司机两辆车能服务四百人的村子，无法服务四千人的山谷。D 项主张推广到每个村庄，与报告的分寸相反；C 项主张给志愿者发薪、B 项说第二辆车是错误，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：报告措辞的分寸
and cannot serve 的限定作用

passages.passage:
Fourteen boats that fish out of the same harbour set up a co-operative in 2016, and it now sells about a fifth of the catch directly to households, at a price that is higher than the auction's and lower than a supermarket's.

The auction is the old arrangement and it is efficient in a manner that has remarkably little to do with fish. A boat lands its catch at four in the morning, a purchaser inspects it and the price is settled within the hour; the fish is subsequently transported two hundred miles and resold. What the auction does not do is tell anybody where the fish came from, and by the time it reaches a shelf it has usually been through three pairs of hands.

The co-operative's version is slower. A boat that intends to sell direct lands with its ice boxes labelled, a member weighs and prices the boxes in a shed beside the quay, and households collect on Friday between four and seven. There is no shop, no delivery service and no card terminal, and the co-operative has twice voted against all three.

What the members did not expect was the argument about price. Selling direct removes the auction's commission and two of the three pairs of hands, and the co-operative could have undercut the supermarkets; instead it set its price above the auction's and put the difference into a fund that pays for engine repairs and a liferaft service. A household that buys a box is, in effect, paying a small premium for the boat to stay in the water.

The scheme has not grown much beyond a fifth of the catch and the chair says that is deliberate. Direct selling takes a member's Friday, the storage shed accommodates only a limited number of boxes, and the co-operative has refused two supermarkets that wanted to buy the whole of it, on the ground that a buyer who takes everything sets the price.

What has altered most is not the revenue but the questions. Members report that purchasers ask which vessel, which ground, which method, and that some of the questions are ones the crew had never been asked and could not answer. The chair says the co-operative's real product is not fish but a name attached to it, and that a name is worth more in a market where nobody else has one.

questions.stem: How much of the catch does the co-operative sell direct?
options: A tenth of it, on Fridays only.
questions.explanation: 首段与第五段都给出同一比例：约五分之一直接卖给家庭。A 项说全部（原文说曾拒绝想包销全部的超商）、D 项说约一半、B 项说十分之一且仅周五，都与原文数字不符。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: about a fifth 的两次出现

questions.stem: What is the auction's chief limitation, according to the passage?
options: It sets prices too high for households.
It operates only in the early morning.
It refuses to sell to supermarkets.
It leaves no trace of where the fish was caught.
questions.answer: It leaves no trace of where the fish was caught.
questions.explanation: 原文明确点出拍卖的短板是“不告诉任何人鱼从哪来”，并经三手转卖后无从追溯。A 项说对家庭定价过高（原文说合作社价高于拍卖价）；B 项说只在清晨营业（那是作业时间而非缺陷）；C 项说拒绝卖给超市，属合作社的行为。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：制度性短板的定位
by the time it reaches a shelf 的推论

questions.stem: Why did the co-operative set its price above the auction's?
options: To pay the chair a salary.
To build a fund for repairs and safety equipment.
questions.answer: To build a fund for repairs and safety equipment.
questions.explanation: 原文说差价进入一个支付发动机维修与救生筏服务的基金，等于让买家为船只继续下海付一小笔溢价。C 项说与超市同价（原文说低于超市）、A 项说给主席发薪、D 项说阻止家庭购买，都与“溢价进入基金”的机制不符。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：定价差异的去向

questions.stem: What is the main function of the last paragraph?
options: To explain how ice boxes are labelled.
To summarise the co-operative's annual accounts.
To identify what the scheme actually sells.
To list the questions crews find hardest.
questions.answer: To identify what the scheme actually sells.
questions.explanation: 该段说变化最大的不是钱而是问题，并借主席之口给出结论：真正的产品不是鱼，而是附着在鱼上的名字。B 项总结年度账目、D 项列举船员最难答的问题、A 项讲冰盒标示，都不是该段落点。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：由现象收束到判断

passages.passage:
A university in the north of England stopped lecturing its first-year engineers in 2019 and gave them problems instead, and the change has been controversial in a way that its designers did not expect.

The lectures had been excellent and almost entirely passive. A hundred and eighty students sat in a hall for fifty minutes, copied a derivation from a screen, and were examined on it in January; the pass rate was high and the failure rate was concentrated, as it always is, among students who had been to a school that taught them how to reproduce rather than how to ask.

The new arrangement gives each group of six a problem and a room, and it gives them no lecture. A demonstrator is present for two hours, and the demonstrator's instruction is to answer a question with a question for the first twenty minutes. The problems are deliberately under-specified: the first one asks a group to design a bridge that will carry a lorry over a stream, and says nothing about the width of the stream or the weight of the lorry.

What the staff underestimated was the cost in time. Preparing a problem takes about ten hours, preparing a lecture took four, and the first year's problems were rewritten twice because groups solved them in ways the designers had not imagined. Six staff who taught on the old course have since left or moved to other units, and the head of the department says the loss was not about the method but about the workload.

The evidence is genuinely mixed. Examination marks in the second year are slightly higher, the number of students who fail the first year has fallen by a third, and the proportion who say they would recommend the course has fallen, because a problem that takes six hours is less pleasant than a lecture that takes one.

The head of department is candid about the last figure. She says students are right to notice that the new course asks more of them, that the department has not solved the staffing problem, and that a university which adopts the method without the ten hours will produce the worst of both arrangements: students who are neither lectured to nor supported, and staff who are asked to invent a course every week.

questions.stem: What did the university replace lectures with?
options: Under-specified problems tackled in small groups.
questions.answer: Under-specified problems tackled in small groups.
questions.explanation: 原文说六人一组、给一个问题和一个房间、不给讲座，且题目刻意“信息不全”。A 项说改成线上录播课、D 项说加长讲座并增员、C 项说每周考试，都与“no lecture”和“under-specified”相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：教学形态的改变

questions.stem: What is the passage's main point about the reform?
options: It has failed and should be abandoned.
Students prefer it to the old course.
Its method works better than its workload allows.
It costs less than the lectures it replaced.
questions.answer: Its method works better than its workload allows.
questions.explanation: 全文的结构是：方法有效（补考率下降三分之一）、代价被低估（备一题十小时、六人流失）、学生推荐度反而下降，末段点明只学方法不给工时会两头落空。A 项说应废止，原文未作此判断；D 项说成本更低（原文说工时更高）；B 项说学生更喜欢，与“推荐比例下降”相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 主旨理解：成效与代价的并置
worst of both arrangements 的收束

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To show that the reform's real cost was staff time.
To describe the bridge-design problem in detail.
To explain how examinations are marked.
questions.answer: To show that the reform's real cost was staff time.
questions.explanation: 该段开门见山说被低估的是时间成本，随后给出十小时对四小时、两次重写、六人离开三组数据。B 项详述桥梁题、C 项比较两组答案、D 项解释阅卷，都不是该段任务，其中 B 项属第三段。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：以数据支撑“成本”论断
ten hours 与 four 的对照

questions.stem: Why does the head of department mention the ten hours?
options: To argue that lectures should be restored.
To warn that adopting the method without the time will fail.
To explain why students recommend the course.
questions.answer: To warn that adopting the method without the time will fail.
questions.explanation: 末段她明说：只学方法不给十小时，会产出“两头最差”的结果。B 项主张恢复讲座，原文未提；A 项为涨学费辩护、D 项解释学生为何推荐，都与该句的警告方向不符，且 D 项本身与“推荐比例下降”矛盾。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：警告性表述的功能

passages.passage:
A consumer group asked two thousand households to list every subscription they paid for, and then asked them, six months later, to list them again without looking at a bank statement; the second list was, on average, two subscriptions short.

The gap is not caused by dishonesty. A subscription is designed to be forgotten: it renews itself, it arrives as a small monthly charge rather than a large annual one, and the service keeps working whether or not anybody uses it. The psychologists who study this call the pattern the "set and forget" problem, and they note that it survives reminders, because a reminder about a service you intended to keep is indistinguishable from one about a service you meant to cancel.

The households in the study were paying, between them, for things they could not name. A quarter held a subscription to a film service they described as "the one with the good documentaries", and a fifth were paying for a storage plan that had been included free with a phone they no longer owned.

What the consumer group found most useful was not the total but the distribution. Households with a written list of their subscriptions spent, on average, thirty per cent less than households without one, and the difference was not explained by income or by the number of people in the house. Writing the list down appeared to be the whole of the intervention.

The group's advice is therefore modest and it is not what a campaign would normally say. It does not recommend cancelling anything; it recommends a page, kept somewhere visible, with the name, the price and the date each subscription renews, and it recommends reading that page in January. The report notes that this is the kind of advice that sounds trivial and is, in the study, worth about two hundred pounds a year.

The most awkward finding is buried in an appendix. Households that cancelled a subscription and then resubscribed within three months — about one in eight — ended up paying more than if they had never cancelled, because the introductory price they had been given the first time was no longer available. The group's chair says she did not expect to be defending the subscription she had just criticised, and that a market which rewards signing up and punishes staying is a market with a problem the consumer cannot solve alone.

questions.stem: What did the second list show?
options: Households had cancelled two subscriptions each.
Households had forgotten about two subscriptions each.
Households paid two pounds more each month.
Households held two fewer services than reported.
questions.answer: Households had forgotten about two subscriptions each.
questions.explanation: 原文说第二份清单平均少列两项，即每户忘掉约两个订阅。A 项说各取消两项（原文未提取消）；C 项说每月多付两镑（数字单位不符）；D 项表述与“少列两项”同义但方向颠倒（不是持有更少，而是记不起来）。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why does the passage say the gap is not caused by dishonesty?
options: Because the households were never asked before.
Because subscriptions are built to be forgotten.
Because the study was badly designed.
questions.answer: Because subscriptions are built to be forgotten.
questions.explanation: 原文随即给出理由：订阅会自动续费、以小额度出现、服务照常运行，因此“忘记”是设计造成的而非有意隐瞒。D 项说银行隐瞒收费、A 项说此前从未被问过、C 项说研究设计糟糕，都在原文中没有依据。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：由机制解释现象

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To explain how the study recruited people.
To identify which single measure made the difference.
To report the households' total spending.
questions.answer: To identify which single measure made the difference.
questions.explanation: 该段说最有用的不是总额而是分布，有清单的家庭少花三成，且差异与收入、人口无关，最后一句点明“写下清单本身就是全部干预”。D 项报总额、C 项比较收入组、A 项讲招募方式，都不是该段任务，其中 C 项恰恰被原文排除。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：从相关到“唯一有效动作”
not explained by income 的排除

questions.stem: Why does the chair mention households who resubscribed?
options: To show the market punishes customers who stay.
To prove that cancelling always saves money.
To argue that the study should be repeated.
To explain how introductory prices are set.
questions.answer: To show the market punishes customers who stay.
questions.explanation: 原文说重新订阅者最终付得更多，因为初次优惠价不再给，主席由此指出市场“奖励新订、惩罚续订”。B 项说取消总能省钱，恰被这一发现推翻；D 项解释优惠价如何设定、C 项主张重做研究，都不是该句用意。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：用反例支撑结构性判断

passages.passage:
Twenty years ago the eastern edge of the city, a stretch of mud that nobody wanted to visit, still held the remains of a chemical works which had dumped waste there for three decades, and the council's plan was to seal the surface with concrete and build a car park above it.

A biologist named Zhou Wen argued instead for something considerably cheaper and slower: to let the water back in. Her proposal was not welcomed by the engineers responsible for the site, who pointed out that a marsh would flood in the rainy season.

Zhou replied with measurements rather than with slogans. A marsh, she explained, retains water the way a sponge does and releases it over several weeks, which is precisely what a city troubled by sudden storms requires. As for the smell, she added, it belongs to water that has lost its oxygen; water which keeps moving does not smell.

The council granted her three years and a modest budget, and local residents were paid to clear rubble and plant reeds along the channels. The first summer produced mosquitoes. The second produced complaints from neighbouring streets. By the third, something had quietly changed: fish had returned to the channels, and with them came herons which had not been recorded in the district since the 1980s.

Samples taken downstream showed a fall in the concentration of heavy metals, not because the marsh filtered them out completely, but because the vegetation slowed the current and allowed sediment to settle.

The most surprising consequence, however, had nothing whatever to do with wildlife. During the floods of 2019, streets two kilometres away remained dry for the first time in living memory. The insurance office calculated that the marsh had saved the city, within a single week, considerably more than its construction had cost.

Not everybody is satisfied. Developers observe that the land could accommodate three thousand flats, and the council continues to debate the value of a park that generates no rent. Zhou, now retired, answers her critics in a manner that visibly unsettles them: you cannot put a price on a place until you have lost it.

Today the site receives school parties every week and appears in the official city guide under a name it never chose for itself, the Breathing Field.

questions.stem: Why did the level of heavy metals fall in the water downstream?
options: The reeds absorbed most of the metal.
Engineers filtered the water before releasing it.
The chemical works was closed down.
Plants made the water slow down, so the mud could settle.
questions.answer: Plants made the water slow down, so the mud could settle.
questions.explanation: 原文用 not because...but because 明确否定了“湿地把重金属全部过滤掉”，指出真正原因是植物让水流变慢、泥沙得以沉降。A 项把“植物吸收”当作原因，属对原文的误读；C 项把化工厂关闭当作原因，原文没有这个时间线；B 项说工程师先行过滤，与原文相反。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：因果与否定结构

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To compare the cost of two plans.
To describe how the marsh was built.
To explain how Zhou defended her idea with evidence.
questions.answer: To explain how Zhou defended her idea with evidence.
questions.explanation: 第三段先用 Zhou replied with measurements rather than with slogans 点出她拿数据说话，再具体解释蓄水原理与气味问题，功能是“用证据反驳质疑”。C 项描述的是第四段的施工过程，位置不对；B 项全段没有比较造价，属无中生有；A 项谈生物学家的专业背景，原文根本没有提及。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：段落在全文中的作用

questions.stem: What does Zhou mean by saying that you cannot put a price on a place until you have lost it?
options: Developers understand prices better than biologists.
The worth of such a place becomes clear only after it is gone.
Land should be sold at a higher price.
Parks always cost more than they return.
questions.answer: The worth of such a place becomes clear only after it is gone.
questions.explanation: 这句话针对的是“这块地能盖三千套房子”的开发商逻辑，意思是价值往往在失去之后才被认识，而不是讨论售价高低。C 项把它读成“该卖更贵”，与反驳开发商的立场相反；A 项说她承认开发商更懂价格，原文没有任何让步；D 项把一句态度表达变成成本论断，也偏离句意。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：作者与人物立场

questions.stem: What happened during the floods of 2019?
questions.explanation: 原文直接写明洪水期间两公里外的街道第一次保持干燥，D 项是该句的同义转述。B 项说湿地受损，原文没有提到任何损害；C 项把 1980 年代后重新出现的鹭鸟说成再次消失，与文意相反；A 项说议会批准建公寓，原文是开发商提出、议会仍在争论。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：时间与事件对应

passages.passage:
Every spring the vocational school on the south bank holds an open day that the academic high schools across the road do not bother to attend. Visitors are shown a workshop where fifteen-year-olds repair electric bicycles, a kitchen where they cost a menu for forty people, and a clinic room where they practise measuring blood pressure on each other. The head, a former factory engineer, is fond of saying that his pupils learn to be useful before they learn to be examined.

That remark has cost him more arguments than any curriculum change. Parents who ring the school usually begin with the same question: will my child still be able to enter a university? The honest answer is yes, though by a narrower door. Roughly a third of the graduates continue into a technical college, and a smaller number sit the same national examination as their academic peers, usually with better results in mathematics than in literature.

What the school cannot promise is status. In the district, a family whose child goes to the vocational school still tends to describe the choice as temporary. Teachers hear the word so often that they have started collecting it: a note on the staff room wall records every time a parent says for now. There are now ninety-four such notes, one for almost every family that has passed through the office this year.

The picture is changing, slowly and unevenly. Factories within twenty kilometres advertise apprenticeships that pay more in the first year than a new graduate earns in an office, and two of them now send engineers to teach on Tuesday afternoons. A pupil who spent last summer servicing air conditioners returned in September able to explain, in three sentences, why a compressor fails.

Whether such evidence will alter the way families talk about the school is another matter. The head concedes that a single open day cannot undo a habit of thought that took thirty years to form. He keeps the door open anyway, and each spring he puts the same sentence at the top of the programme: the point of an education is not to postpone life.

questions.stem: What can visitors see on the open day?
options: A laboratory where pupils test drinking water.
A workshop where pupils repair electric bicycles.
A garden where pupils grow vegetables.
An office where pupils learn bookkeeping.
questions.answer: A workshop where pupils repair electric bicycles.
questions.explanation: 原文在介绍开放日时明确列出三个场所，第一个就是学生修理电动自行车的车间。A 项的净水检测、D 项的记账、C 项的菜园，原文都没有出现，属于把“职业学校”想当然地补上其他专业。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：列举信息定位

questions.stem: Why does the head's remark cause arguments?
options: It compares two groups of teachers.
It promises every graduate a well-paid job.
It criticises the academic schools across the road.
It suggests that examinations matter less than practical skill.
questions.answer: It suggests that examinations matter less than practical skill.
questions.explanation: 这句话把 useful 排在 examined 之前，等于把考试放在次要位置，而 district 里的家长恰恰最在意升学，冲突由此产生。C 项说他在批评对面的普通高中，原文只说那些学校不来参加开放日，没有评价；B 项承诺高薪工作，原文只说第一年学徒工资高于办公室新人；A 项比较两类教师，原文没有这层意思。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 句意理解：比较结构的含义

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To explain why parents distrust the school.
To compare wages in two industries.
To describe how apprenticeships are organised.
To offer evidence that the school's prospects are improving.
questions.answer: To offer evidence that the school's prospects are improving.
questions.explanation: 该段开头即说 The picture is changing，随后用工厂招学徒、派工程师来上课、学生能解释压缩机故障三个事实支撑这一判断，功能是“为变化提供证据”。C 项谈学徒制的组织方式，原文只提到工资与授课，没有制度细节；B 项把两种工资的对比当成段落主旨，那只是证据之一；A 项说解释家长为何不信任，方向与该段相反。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：段落在全文中的作用

questions.stem: What does the head mean by saying that the point of an education is not to postpone life?
options: Learning should not merely delay a pupil's real life.
The school will close if parents remain unconvinced.
Parents are to blame for the school's reputation.
Vocational training should replace academic study.
questions.answer: Learning should not merely delay a pupil's real life.
questions.explanation: postpone life 指把真正的生活一再往后推，这句话是在反驳“读书只是为了延迟进入社会”的观念，强调学习本身就该有用。D 项把态度读成“取代普通教育”，语气过强，原文仍承认学生可以考大学；B 项说学校会关门，原文没有任何这样的判断；C 项把一句教育主张变成对家长的指责，也偏离句意。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：句子背后的主张
修辞理解：postpone life 的含义

passages.passage:
A hundred kilometres west of the city, in a valley where the bamboo grows straight and thin, one family still makes paper the way it did four hundred years ago. The work begins before dawn, when the bamboo is cut, soaked and beaten into a pulp that looks, at first, like grey porridge. Nothing about the process is quick: a single sheet takes eleven days, and a worker who has done it for thirty years can still be heard complaining that the weather has spoiled a batch, and the family plans its year around the seasons that will and will not cooperate.

For most of the twentieth century the paper sold itself. Schools bought it for calligraphy lessons, and the workshop employed twenty-two people. Then, in the 1990s, machines in the north began producing a cheaper sheet, and within a decade the workshop was down to three workers, all of them over fifty.

The revival, when it came, arrived from an unexpected direction. A designer in the city ordered a small quantity for an exhibition, and photographs of the textured surface travelled faster than any advertisement could have. Orders now arrive from bookbinders, from museums repairing scrolls, and from a handful of young artists who pay for the irregularities that machines cannot copy. The family has taken on six apprentices, the first in a generation.

Not everything has been preserved. The workshop now uses a small electric pump, and the eldest son admits that the old foot-powered bellows were romantic only in photographs. What has not changed is the number of decisions a maker must take in a single morning, judging the thickness of the pulp by the sound it makes against the mould.

Visitors often ask whether the craft can survive. The answer given by the family is neither gloomy nor confident: as long as someone is willing to wait eleven days for a sheet of paper, the valley will keep making it. What worries them is not the machines but the silence in the village school, where calligraphy is now taught once a term, if at all.

questions.stem: What happened to the workshop in the 1990s?
options: Machines in the north made a cheaper sheet, and the workshop shrank.
The family sold the business to a museum.
Schools stopped buying paper for calligraphy.
The workshop moved to a larger valley.
questions.answer: Machines in the north made a cheaper sheet, and the workshop shrank.
questions.explanation: 原文直接写明 1990 年代北方机器开始生产更便宜的纸，十年内作坊只剩三名工人，B 项与 D 项在原文中都没有出现，属虚构；C 项把学校不再购买当作原因，原文说的是机器带来的价格竞争，学校购买是在此之前的事。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：时间与事件对应

questions.stem: What brought the first new orders to the workshop?
options: Photographs of the paper shown in a city exhibition.
A museum that needed cheap packing material.
A government programme for traditional crafts.
An advertisement placed in a national newspaper.
questions.answer: Photographs of the paper shown in a city exhibition.
questions.explanation: 原文说设计师为展览订购了一小批，纸张纹理的照片传播得比任何广告都快，可见带来订单的是这些照片。C 项的政策扶持、B 项的廉价包装材料、D 项的报纸广告原文都没有提到；原文恰恰说效果比广告更好，把广告当成原因属反向理解。因此答案是 B。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To list the machines the workshop has bought.
To explain why young artists prefer handmade paper.
To separate what has changed from what has stayed the same.
To describe the village school's calligraphy lessons.
questions.answer: To separate what has changed from what has stayed the same.
questions.explanation: 该段先用 Not everything has been preserved 承认变化，再用 What has not changed 说明保留了什么，功能是“分清变与不变”。A 项只提到一台电泵，不足以概括全段；B 项谈年轻艺术家为何偏爱手工纸，属第三段内容；D 项把村小学的书法课放在这里，位置不对。因此答案是 B。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：对比结构的段落

questions.stem: What worries the family most?
options: The shortage of apprentices in the valley.
Competition from factories in the north.
The loss of interest among village children.
questions.answer: The loss of interest among village children.
questions.explanation: 原文用 not...but 结构明确指出，让他们担心的不是机器，而是村小学里书法一学期才上一次课这件事，指向下一代对手写与纸张的疏远。A 项的竹子成本、B 项的学徒短缺原文都没有提，而且原文说已收了六名学徒；C 项的工厂竞争正是他们说“不担心”的那一项。因此答案是 B。

passages.passage:
For one Sunday a month the community hall becomes a repair cafe, and the people who arrive first are rarely the ones who need it most. They are the retired engineers, who claim the tables by the window and spend the first hour arguing about which of them is responsible for the kettle that failed in November, and the quarrel is never really about kettles, which nobody there has thrown away in a decade.

The rule is printed on a card at every table: you stay while your object is fixed, and you watch. Nothing is repaired behind a curtain, and nothing leaves the building in worse condition than it arrived. A student volunteer who expected to be handed a screwdriver and a broken radio learned on her first visit that she would spend forty minutes listening to an explanation of why the radio's transformer had failed.

Most of what comes through the door is small. Lamps with loose wires, toasters that no longer heat, a sewing machine whose timing is a fraction of a millimetre out, which took two visits to settle and taught everyone present more than a manual would have. The volunteers say that perhaps one object in five cannot be saved, usually because a part is no longer manufactured, and that this proportion has stayed remarkably steady over six years.

What has changed is who brings things in. In the first year the queue was almost entirely people over sixty, many of whom had repaired the same appliances when they were young. Now roughly a third of the visitors are under thirty, and a few arrive with objects they have bought precisely because they look repairable.

The volunteers are suspicious of this attention and pleased by it at the same time. One of them, who spent thirty years servicing lifts, points out that a repair cafe cannot compete with a factory: it can only delay the moment at which a thing is thrown away. He keeps coming anyway, because, as he puts it, a person who has watched a toaster come back to life treats the next toaster differently.

questions.stem: What must a visitor do at the repair cafe?
options: Explain the fault to a committee first.
Pay a fixed fee before the work starts.
Stay and watch while the object is mended.
Leave the object and collect it later.
questions.answer: Stay and watch while the object is mended.
questions.explanation: 卡片上的规则说得很清楚：修的时候人要在场，并且看着。B 项收费、D 项留下物件稍后取、A 项先向委员会说明，原文都没有这些安排——原文恰恰说“不在帘子后面修”，就是要求当面。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：规则条款定位

questions.stem: Why do some young visitors bring objects that look repairable?
options: They are required to by a school project.
They intend to mend them rather than replace them.
They hope to sell them to the volunteers.
They want to test whether the cafe is real.
questions.answer: They intend to mend them rather than replace them.
questions.explanation: “特意因为看起来能修才买”说明这些人买的时候就打算修，而不是用完就丢。C 项倒卖、A 项学校项目、D 项试探真假，原文都没有依据；D 项尤其与“他们带着自家物件来修”的语境不符。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To argue that old appliances were better made.
To list the tools the volunteers use.
To explain why lamps are more common than toasters.
To show how modest most repairs are and how often they fail.
questions.answer: To show how modest most repairs are and how often they fail.
questions.explanation: 该段先列举的都是小物件（台灯、烤面包机、缝纫机），再给出“五分之一救不回来”且比例六年不变，功能是说明修复的规模有限、失败率稳定。B 项工具清单原文没有；C 项比较台灯与烤面包机的数量，原文只并列；A 项“老电器做得更好”是另一层判断，原文没作此评价。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：段落在全文中的作用

questions.stem: What does the lift engineer believe about the cafe?
options: It exists mainly to train young engineers.
It can only postpone disposal, but it changes how people treat things.
It will soon be able to compete with factories.
It should refuse objects that are not repairable.
questions.answer: It can only postpone disposal, but it changes how people treat things.
questions.explanation: 他一方面承认修不好产业，只能把丢弃的时刻往后推；另一方面正因为“看过烤面包机复活的人会不一样”而继续来，两句合起来就是选项的意思。C 项说要与工厂竞争，原文说他明确认为竞争不了；D 项拒收不可修的物件，原文反而是照实告知；A 项培训青年工程师，原文没有这层功能。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：让步与坚持并存
句意理解：as he puts it

passages.passage:
Every Thursday evening a club of amateur runners gathers at the edge of the industrial estate, where the roads are flat, the lorries have gone home, and the streetlights come on before the warm-up is over. Their coach, a former teacher of physical education, has one rule he refuses to soften: nobody runs the first kilometre faster than the last.

The rule is unpopular with newcomers, most of whom arrive believing that the point of a run is to empty themselves. One of them, an accountant who had finished two marathons, lasted three weeks before asking whether the club was serious. He was told that a runner who starts too fast spends the rest of the evening paying for it, and that the payment is not always visible on the same day. The accountant now runs his first kilometre at a pace he would once have called walking, and has stopped counting the days he missed, which he now regards as progress of a kind.

Watches make the argument harder to settle. A device will report a pace of five minutes per kilometre and say nothing about the two days afterwards when the calf refuses to work. The coach therefore asks his members to keep a second record, in a notebook, of how they felt the following morning, and he reads that more carefully than the numbers.

The club has grown from nine members to forty in four years, and the coach attributes this less to enthusiasm than to injury. Most people who take up running stop within a year, he says, and the commonest reason is not laziness but a body that was never given time to adapt. He has also noticed that the members who stay are those who arrive with a question rather than a target.

What the club sells, in the end, is patience. Nothing about it is fast, including the improvement. A member who took eleven minutes off his half-marathon time did so over two seasons, and the coach remembers the day the man stopped chasing a personal best and started finishing every run still able to talk.

questions.stem: What is the coach's rule?
options: The first kilometre must not be the fastest.
New members must run alone for a month.
Every run must end with a sprint.
questions.answer: The first kilometre must not be the fastest.
questions.explanation: 原句说不许第一公里比最后一公里快，等于要求起跑不能最快。D 项以冲刺收尾，原文说的是“不能比起步快”，并没有要求冲刺；C 项单独跑一个月、B 项记录每一公里都不是这条规则的内容（记录在第三段，是另一件事）。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：规则的同义转换

questions.stem: Why does the coach read the notebook more carefully than the numbers?
options: It records damage that a pace reading cannot show.
It contains the club's race results.
It is written by the faster members.
It is the only record the club keeps.
questions.answer: It records damage that a pace reading cannot show.
questions.explanation: 手表能给配速，却说不清两天后小腿为何罢工，笔记本记的正是第二天早晨的身体感受，所以更可信。C 项说由快的人写、B 项说装着比赛成绩、D 项说这是唯一记录，原文都不成立——第三段明说还有手表数据，是“第二份记录”。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：两类数据的差别
指代关系：that 指笔记本

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To argue that running is bad for the body.
To compare the club with a professional team.
To explain that the club grew by preventing injury rather than by inspiring enthusiasm.
To describe the route the club uses.
questions.answer: To explain that the club grew by preventing injury rather than by inspiring enthusiasm.
questions.explanation: 该段开头用 less...than 明确把增长归因于“少受伤”而不是“热情”，随后用“多数人一年内放弃、原因不是懒而是身体没时间适应”支撑。B 项与职业队比较、D 项描述路线，原文都没有；A 项说跑步伤身，是把“没给身体适应时间”读成否定跑步本身。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：因果段的作用

questions.stem: What does the coach value most in a run?
options: Finishing with enough breath to talk.
Running a fixed pace from start to finish.
Breaking a personal best every season.
questions.answer: Finishing with enough breath to talk.
questions.explanation: 末句把“不再追个人最好成绩、跑完还能说话”作为值得记住的转折，说明教练看重的是留有余力的跑法。C 项恰恰是他不再追的东西；B 项匀速原文只说起步不能最快，没有要求全程定速；D 项与快的人同练，原文没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：转折句的价值判断

passages.passage:
For one week each term the canteen of a secondary school in the south weighs everything that comes back from the tables. The total is written on a board by the door, and in the first year it was published the number was so large that two teachers assumed the scale was broken. Nobody remembers who first proposed publishing it, and the dietician insists that the idea was merely borrowed from a hospital ward.

Weighing was not the school's own idea. It came from a hospital dietician who had spent a decade telling patients what to eat and had concluded that advice without measurement changes nothing. She proposed the board, and the head, who had expected resistance from the kitchen, found almost none: the staff asked for the weekly figures before the board was even updated, and the head began quoting them in assembly.

What changed first was not the cooking but the portions. Students began taking less of the dishes they knew they would leave, and the kitchen, seeing what came back untouched, stopped offering two of them altogether. Within a term the waste had fallen by a third, and no dish had become less popular; the cook in charge still keeps the old menu on the wall, crossed out rather than removed, as a record of what the school used to serve, before the weighing began.

The second change was quieter and harder to measure. A group of students asked to weigh the waste themselves at the end of each day, and the figures they produced were slightly lower than the kitchen's. The difference was small, but the students argued that a number you produce yourself is a number you are willing to defend.

Not everyone is convinced. A teacher of economics points out that the board measures what is thrown away, not what is eaten well, and that a student can always reduce waste by eating less, which moves the problem out of the canteen and into the afternoon. The dietician accepts the objection, and answers that the board was never meant to be a verdict, only a mirror.

questions.stem: What was the teachers' first reaction to the number on the board?
options: They doubted the scale was working.
They compared it with another school's figure.
They asked for the board to be removed.
questions.answer: They doubted the scale was working.
questions.explanation: 原文说数字太大，两位老师以为秤坏了，这就是对设备的怀疑。C 项责怪厨房、D 项要求撤掉板子、B 项与他校比较，原文都没有出现，而且后文说校长原本预期厨房会抵触，结果几乎没人反对，与“责怪”相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：人物反应定位

questions.stem: Why did the waste fall without any dish becoming less popular?
options: Students were told to eat less at lunch.
The kitchen began cooking different food.
The board was removed after one term.
Portions shrank and two unpopular dishes were dropped.
questions.answer: Portions shrank and two unpopular dishes were dropped.
questions.explanation: 学生少拿自己知道会剩的菜，厨房又停做两样没人动的菜，两边合起来就是“份量变小＋撤掉不受欢迎的菜”，而原文特意说“没有哪道菜变得不受欢迎”。A 项要求学生少吃，原文说的是少拿会剩的；B 项换菜谱，与“停做两样”不同；C 项撤板子是另一回事。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：两个原因合并

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To prove that the kitchen's numbers were wrong.
To compare two groups of teachers.
To describe how the board was built.
To show students taking over the measuring and trusting their own figures.
questions.answer: To show students taking over the measuring and trusting their own figures.
questions.explanation: 该段写学生自己称、数字略低、并强调“自己算出的数才愿意为之辩护”，功能是从“被动看板子”转为“自己掌握测量”。A 项说证明厨房数据错了，原文只说略低、差别很小，没有指控；C 项讲板子怎么造，原文没写；B 项比较两组老师，本段主体是学生。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：段落的推进作用

questions.stem: What does the dietician mean by calling the board a mirror?
options: It reflects behaviour without passing judgement.
It shows other schools how much they waste.
It records only the food that is eaten.
questions.answer: It reflects behaviour without passing judgement.
questions.explanation: 镜子只照出样子、不下判决，与前半句 not a verdict 对照，说明板子是把情况照给人看，而不是评判谁。B 项与他校比较、C 项让学生羞愧、D 项只记吃掉的food，都与“mirror/verdict”这组对照不符。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 对照结构：not a verdict, only a mirror

passages.passage:
The bus station closed in 2009, and for eleven years the building stood empty, its departure boards still showing routes to villages that no longer had a bus. When a theatre company, unable to afford a permanent stage, asked whether it could use the concourse, the council agreed within a fortnight, largely because the alternative was to keep paying for an empty building.

What the company built there is not a conventional theatre. The audience sits on the old benches, which are bolted to the floor, and the actors perform where the ticket machines used to stand. There is no curtain, and the lighting comes from twelve lamps hung from the roof beams by a retired electrician who now works front of house.

The first production was chosen for reasons of cost: a play with four characters and a single room. It sold out for six weeks, largely to people who had never been to the theatre in their lives, who came because the building belonged to them, a fact the artistic director admits was luck rather than deliberate policy.

Since then the company has kept a rule that no play may need more scenery than three people can carry through the doors. The rule has produced a style that critics call spare and audiences call clear, because a chair, a table and a lamp must do the work that a painted forest once did. The rule also decides which plays can be staged at all, and two scripts have been rejected on that ground alone.

Funding remains a difficulty, as it does for every company outside the capital, and the council provides the building and nothing else, tickets are kept below the price of a cinema seat, and the actors are paid per performance rather than per week. A single full-time administrator handles everything else.

What is harder to measure is the effect on the town, where a teacher who brings a class every term reports that students who have watched a play in a bus station read plays differently, because they have seen how little a stage needs. The artistic director puts it more simply: a theatre with no wings teaches an audience to watch rather than to be impressed.

questions.stem: What does the council provide for the theatre company?
questions.explanation: 原文说议会只提供建筑、别的一概不给，正好对应“给房子不给钱”。C 项说每年更新的拨款，原文只提到剧团靠一笔年度拨款生存，来源并未说是议会；D 项说演员的工资，原文明确演员按场付费；B 项说给学校的免费票，原文只提到老师带班来看。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：供给内容定位

questions.stem: Why did the first production sell out?
options: Because tickets were given away free.
Because the company had a national reputation.
Because the play was written by a famous author.
Because local people felt the building was theirs.
questions.answer: Because local people felt the building was theirs.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说观众大多从没进过剧院，来是因为这栋楼属于他们，即“这是我们的地方”。C 项说名作家写的，原文只说是为省钱选的四个角色的戏；A 项说免费送票，原文说票价低于电影票而不是白送；B 项说剧团全国知名，原文强调它请不起固定舞台。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To describe the theatre's ticket prices.
To argue that painted scenery is old-fashioned.
To explain how a rule about scenery shaped the company's style.
questions.answer: To explain how a rule about scenery shaped the company's style.
questions.explanation: 该段先给出“布景不许超过三个人能搬动”这条规则，再说它带来了“简省”与“清楚”的风格，功能是说明规则如何塑造风格。B 项票价属第五段；A 项把评论家与观众并列，那只是风格的两个形容；C 项说画出来的森林过时，原文只把它当作对照。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：规则与结果的关系

questions.stem: What does the artistic director value most?
options: A large audience from outside the town.
An audience that watches closely rather than one that is impressed.
Plays written by the company itself.
questions.answer: An audience that watches closely rather than one that is impressed.
questions.explanation: 末句把 watch 与 be impressed 对立起来，说明他要的是专注观看而不是被场面震住。A 项要外地大观众群，原文强调观众是本镇的人；C 项要逼真的昂贵布景，恰恰与他“三人能搬动”的规则相反；D 项自编剧目，原文没有这层意思。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：对立结构的含义

passages.passage:
A careers adviser who has worked with sixteen-year-olds for twenty years says the most useful question she asks has changed. It used to be what do you want to be; now it is what would you be willing to do badly for two years.

The change came from watching a pattern among several hundred former students, and the pattern was consistent: those who chose a career because it sounded impressive tended to leave it within three years, often describing the work as not what they had imagined. Those who chose something they were willing to be bad at, at least at first, stayed longer and complained less. Some of them, she notes, had been advised by adults who meant well and who mistook enthusiasm for evidence.

She now runs an exercise in which a class lists three activities they lose track of time doing, and then works out what those activities have in common. The answers are rarely dramatic: repairing things, explaining things, organising other people's disorder. What surprises the students is how specific the pattern becomes once it is written down.

Employers, she says, are less interested in the answer itself than in the reasoning that produced it. A candidate who can explain why he chose a subject, and what he did when it turned out to be harder than expected, tells an interviewer more than a list of grades does.

Her advice is unpopular with some parents, who point out that the labour market rewards qualifications and that a sixteen-year-old cannot know what he will enjoy at thirty. She accepts the first point and disputes the second: most people, she argues, are not choosing a job for life but a first job, and a first job is a place to learn how work is done. She adds that such a job teaches punctuality, cooperation and how to be corrected, none of which an interview can test.

What she hopes to prevent is the particular misery of a young person who has done everything that was asked of him and still cannot say what he is for. The alternative, she says, is a generation that is qualified and uncertain.

questions.stem: What is the adviser's new question?
options: What subject do you enjoy most at school?
Which activity would you accept doing badly for a while?
What do your parents want you to become?
Which career pays the most in ten years?
questions.answer: Which activity would you accept doing badly for a while?
questions.explanation: 原文直接给出新旧两个问题，新问题即“你愿意在两年里把什么做得很差”。A 项问最喜欢的科目、D 项问十年后的收入、C 项问父母的期望，原文都没有把它们作为核心问题；D 项尤其与她对“听起来体面”的批评相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：新旧对比定位

questions.stem: Why did students who chose impressive careers leave them?
options: The pay was lower than they had been promised.
The work did not match what they had imagined.
They had no qualifications for the job.
They were asked to move to another city.
questions.answer: The work did not match what they had imagined.
questions.explanation: 原文说他们离开时常说“这工作和想象的不一样”，即期待与现实的落差。A 项薪水低于承诺、D 项被要求搬到别的城市、C 项没有资历，原文都没有出现；C 项尤其与“他们选了这份职业”矛盾。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To list the activities students most often choose.
To prove that repairing things is the best job.
To show how an exercise turns vague interests into a visible pattern.
To compare two classes in different schools.
questions.answer: To show how an exercise turns vague interests into a visible pattern.
questions.explanation: 该段描述练习过程并用“写下来之后模式变得很具体”收尾，功能是说明练习如何把模糊兴趣变成可辨认的模式。A 项只列举活动，那是过程的一部分而非目的；B 项断言修东西是最好的职业，属于过度推断；D 项比较两个班，原文没有。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: How does the adviser answer parents who say a teenager cannot know what he will enjoy at thirty?
options: She accepts both points without reservation.
She agrees about qualifications but says a first job is mainly a place to learn.
She argues that teenagers change jobs every year.
She says parents should choose for their children.
questions.answer: She agrees about qualifications but says a first job is mainly a place to learn.
questions.explanation: 原文说接受第一点（文凭有用）但不同意第二点，理由是大家选的是第一份工作而不是终身职业。A 项说两点全接受，与 disputes 矛盾；C 项说青少年每年换工作，原文无此说法；D 项说让父母替孩子选，与她的立场相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：部分接受与反驳

passages.passage:
Few failures of memory are as embarrassing as forgetting a name that was given to you thirty seconds earlier. A team of psychologists who have spent four years on the problem report that the difficulty is rarely storage; it is attention. The experience is so common that most people assume it is a defect either of age or of memory itself, and because they assume that, they make no attempt to change what they do at the moment a name is given.
