In their experiments volunteers met a stranger, heard a name, and were then asked a question about something else. Those who were asked to repeat the name silently remembered it far more often than those who had merely heard it clearly. The difference was not intelligence or effort but the small act of rehearsal. The experiment was repeated with a second name introduced two minutes later, and the same pattern appeared among volunteers who had earlier described themselves, without much embarrassment, as hopeless with names.

The second finding was less obvious. When volunteers were told that they would be tested on the name, they remembered it; when they were told they would not be tested, they did not, even though both groups had heard it equally clearly. Expecting to need something appears to be part of learning it.

The team is careful about what this means. It does not follow that people with poor memories are careless, or that a technique will undo a habit formed over decades. What follows is narrower and more useful: attention is a resource that can be spent deliberately, and most of us spend it on the wrong thing during an introduction.

Their practical suggestion is unglamorous. Say the name back once, use it in a sentence within the first minute, and accept that you will sometimes fail. The last part matters, they argue, because the fear of forgetting makes people avoid introductions altogether, which guarantees the failure they dread. None of this makes an introduction comfortable, and the team does not pretend that a technique will remove the awkwardness of meeting someone whose name you may forget before the sentence ends.

questions.stem: What do the psychologists say is the usual problem?
questions.explanation: 原文用 rarely storage; it is attention 明确把原因归于注意力。A 项把两者颠倒，正是原文否定的说法；B 项听力困难、C 项词汇不足，原文都没有提到，实验里所有人听到的清晰度相同。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why did the group expecting a test remember better?
options: They had better hearing than the other group.
Expecting to need the name seems to help learning.
They were told the name twice as often.
They were given more time to listen.
questions.answer: Expecting to need the name seems to help learning.
questions.explanation: 两组听得同样清楚，唯一差别是是否预期被考，结论自然是“预期需要”本身促进记忆。D 项时间更多、A 项听力更好、C 项听了两遍，原文明确说两组听到的清晰度相同，因此都排除。答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To describe the volunteers in detail.
To limit what the findings can be taken to prove.
To explain why names are important.
questions.answer: To limit what the findings can be taken to prove.
questions.explanation: 该段用 It does not follow 连否两个可能的误读，再给出“更窄也更有用”的结论，功能是给结论划界。A 项细描志愿者、D 项批评其他团队、C 项说明名字为何重要，都不是该段做的事；C 项尤其属第一段的引入。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：限定结论范围
It does not follow 的论证作用

questions.stem: Why do the psychologists think it matters to accept occasional failure?
options: Failure proves that memory cannot be trained.
Names are less important than faces.
Fear of failing makes people avoid introductions, which causes the failure.
Apologising is a way to start a conversation.
questions.answer: Fear of failing makes people avoid introductions, which causes the failure.
questions.explanation: 原文说怕忘就干脆回避介绍，而回避恰好保证了他们所怕的失败，这是接受偶尔失败的意义。A 项说失败证明记忆无法训练，与他们给出方法相反；D 项说道歉可以开启对话，原文没提；B 项说名字不如面孔重要，原文无此比较。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：因果链的完整理解

passages.passage:
When a friend describes a problem, most of us answer with a suggestion. A study of ordinary conversations found that advice arrived, on average, within nineteen seconds of the complaint, and that the person with the difficulty usually stopped talking soon afterwards.

The researchers are careful not to blame the advisers. Offering a solution is a way of showing concern, and it is far quicker than sitting with someone else's difficulty. What the study measured, though, was not how useful the advice turned out to be but whether the conversation continued, and that is a narrower question than the one most advice-givers believe they are answering.

In the conversations that lasted, the listener did three things in a fixed order: repeating the last few words, asking a question with no solution inside it, and waiting. None of these is difficult, and all of them feel slow. The advice, when it came at last, was shorter, and the speakers described those conversations as more useful even when nothing had been decided.

There is a practical reason for the sequence. Advice given before a person has finished describing the problem is advice about the wrong problem, because the first version of a difficulty is rarely the true one. A colleague who complains about a deadline may really be describing a disagreement with a manager, and the suggestion that repairs the timetable will not touch the disagreement at all.

The finding that surprised the team was how much people wanted to be asked, and how rarely the wish was granted. In a follow-up questionnaire the most valued question was not the cleverest but the simplest, namely what would help most, and almost nobody reported having been asked it.

What the study does not claim is that listening is a technique for getting one's way. The listeners who waited often heard things that required them to act, and some of the conversations ended with a request that could not decently be refused, which is a cost the technique does not advertise and few of the books on listening bother to mention it.

questions.stem: What did the study find about advice in ordinary conversations?
options: It was longer than the complaint itself.
It was offered only when it was asked for.
It usually arrived within about nineteen seconds.
questions.answer: It usually arrived within about nineteen seconds.
questions.explanation: 原文明确给出平均数十九秒。C 项说只有被请求时才给建议，原文说几乎没人被问过需要什么；B 项说建议比抱怨更长，原文说后来的建议反而更短；A 项说建议多来自陌生人，原文谈的是朋友之间。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why is advice given too early described as advice about the wrong problem?
options: Because the first account of a difficulty is seldom the real one.
Because listeners forget what they have heard.
questions.answer: Because the first account of a difficulty is seldom the real one.
questions.explanation: 原文用 because 直接给出理由：最初那版描述很少是真实的那一个。D 项说听者忘了内容、A 项说建议总是不受欢迎、B 项说问题多半是想象的，原文都没有支持，其中 A 项与“建议是表达关心的方式”矛盾。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To compare two groups of professional advisers.
To describe the sequence of moves that kept conversations going.
To list the questions listeners should never ask.
To explain why waiting is a waste of time.
questions.answer: To describe the sequence of moves that kept conversations going.
questions.explanation: 该段先给出三个按顺序发生的动作，再说这些做法带来的结果，功能是描述“让对话继续”的一组做法。C 项说列出不该问的问题，原文只给了一个应问的问题；A 项比较两组专业顾问，原文没有分组；D 项说等待浪费时间，与“那些对话被评价为更有用”相反。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What does the team refuse to claim about listening?
options: That it is a trick for getting what you want.
That listening takes more time than advice.
That advisers are usually well meaning.
questions.answer: That it is a trick for getting what you want.
questions.explanation: 原文明确否定的正是“倾听是得手的手段”这一说法。C 项说倾听比建议更费时，原文承认它慢，但那是事实陈述而非拒绝的主张；D 项说建议者多半出于好意，原文正是这么说的；B 项说有些对话收场不佳，原文也承认。因此答案是 A。

passages.passage:
A price that ends in ninety-nine pence looks like a gimmick, and it has survived a century of retailing. The usual explanation is that customers read from left to right and stop at the first digit, so that 3.99 feels closer to three pounds than to four.

That explanation is only half true, and the half that is false matters. Experiments in which the same price is written as 3.99 and as 4.00 do find a difference, but a small one, and it disappears when the buyer is given time to think or when the purchase is repeated. The effect is strongest for unfamiliar goods bought quickly, and weakest for the weekly shopping, where the total is felt rather than read.

The other half of the story is about the shop rather than the customer. A price ending in ninety-nine makes the drawer easier to count, gives the assistant a reason to hand back change, and creates the impression that the figure was calculated rather than chosen. Supermarkets discovered long ago that customers who receive change are more likely to spend it on something small before they leave.

There is a cost to the convention. A shop that prices everything this way cannot raise a price by ten pence without breaking the pattern, and customers notice when the ninety-nines vanish. One chain that abandoned the habit for a year reported that sales of its cheapest line fell by nine per cent, although the price itself was unchanged and no customer could have explained why.

Economists who study this are divided about whether it should count as a trick. The conservative view is that it is information: a buyer who knows the convention is not deceived, only hurried. The other view is that a price designed to be misread is a small dishonesty which the market tolerates because everybody uses it.

What both sides agree on is narrower than either would like. The ninety-nine does not make people buy things they do not want; it makes them buy slightly sooner, and slightly sooner is where most retail profit is made.

questions.stem: What is the usual explanation for prices ending in ninety-nine?
options: Customers stop reading at the first digit.
Shops want to give change quickly.
questions.answer: Customers stop reading at the first digit.
questions.explanation: 原文把常见解释归结为“从左往右读、看到第一位数字就停”。C 项说店主想快点找零，那是第三段提出的另一半原因；B 项说税制要求、D 项说便于盘库，原文都没有提。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：常见解释定位

questions.stem: Why do shops like prices that produce change?
options: It discourages customers from paying by card.
It reduces the time staff spend at the till.
Customers tend to spend the change on something small.
It keeps the shelves looking tidy.
questions.answer: Customers tend to spend the change on something small.
questions.explanation: 原文说拿到零钱的顾客更容易在离店前买点小东西，这正是店家乐见的结果。B 项说减少结账时间，原文反而强调找零这个动作；D 项说货架整齐、A 项说抑制刷卡，原文未提。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To prove that customers cannot count.
To shift the explanation from the buyer's perception to the shop's operation.
To describe how prices are printed.
questions.answer: To shift the explanation from the buyer's perception to the shop's operation.
questions.explanation: 该段开头一句就把视角从顾客转到店铺，随后列出三条与经营有关的理由，功能是补上另一半解释。A 项说证明顾客不会算数，原文并未这样断言；D 项说描述印价方式、B 项说抨击超市不诚实，都不是该段主旨。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What do the two camps of economists agree on?
options: Customers are always deceived by such prices.
Such prices should be banned by law.
The convention has no measurable effect.
Such prices make people buy sooner, not buy unwanted things.
questions.answer: Such prices make people buy sooner, not buy unwanted things.
questions.explanation: 末段明确指出两派都同意的范围很窄：价格不让人买不需要的东西，只让人买得早一点。B 项要求立法禁止，原文没有主张；A 项说顾客总被骗，那是其中一派的观点而非共识；C 项说没有可测效果，与“实验确实发现差异”矛盾。因此答案是 A。

passages.passage:
A regional newspaper began printing its errors on the front page in 2019, in a box deliberately placed above the fold and set in the same type as the headlines. The editor expected complaints from advertisers; what arrived instead was a small but steady rise in subscriptions.

The reasoning behind the box was practical rather than moral. Corrections buried on page nine were read by almost nobody, which meant that the people most affected by an error never saw it put right, and their letters to the office grew angrier every year.

The box has rules. It names the error, states what is correct, and says how the mistake happened: a wrong figure taken from a press release, a name misspelled because the reporter trusted an old directory, a photograph used without anyone checking its date. Only the third kind has proved embarrassing, and the editor argues that this is exactly the point.

What the paper has lost is the appearance of confidence. A rival editor told a trade magazine that the box teaches readers to doubt everything else, and that a paper admitting three errors a week cannot also expect to be trusted when it investigates the council.

The answer from the newsroom is that trust was never produced by silence. A reader who sees a correction about a street name knows that the paper checks street names; a reader who sees no corrections learns only that the paper has decided not to look. The paper now prints a quarterly tally, which is a shorter list than its rivals would care to publish, and it prints the number of complaints it has rejected as well.

After four years the box has become the most read feature in the paper, and the editor has noticed a change in what readers write in about. The letters are less often about the paper being wrong and more often about the paper being incomplete, which is a harder charge to answer and, she says, a better one, because it can be answered with reporting rather than with apology, and the reporting takes several weeks.

questions.stem: What did the editor expect when the box was introduced?
questions.explanation: 原文说编辑预料广告商会抱怨，实际来的却是订阅量小幅上升。D 项说订阅上升，那是实际结果而非预期；A 项说新闻编辑室抗议、B 项说议会来信，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why were corrections previously buried on page nine?
options: Because almost nobody read them there, so those affected never saw them.
Because page nine was reserved for advertising.
questions.answer: Because almost nobody read them there, so those affected never saw them.
questions.explanation: 原文把“几乎无人读”与“受影响的人看不到更正”连成因果，这正是问题所在。D 项说第九版留给广告、C 项说法律要求、A 项说读者偏好短版，原文均无依据。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To compare the paper with a rival.
To explain how photographs are chosen.
To list the paper's most popular stories.
To show what the box discloses and which kind of error is most damaging.
questions.answer: To show what the box discloses and which kind of error is most damaging.
questions.explanation: 该段先列出三条规则，再点出第三类错误最令人难堪，功能是说明公开的内容与最伤人的那一类。C 项最受欢迎的报道、A 项与对手比较、B 项选照片的方法，都不是该段主旨，其中 A 项属下一段。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: How does the editor answer the charge that the box teaches readers to doubt everything?
options: Readers do not notice corrections at all.
The charge is correct and the box will be removed.
Trust comes from visible checking, not from silence.
questions.answer: Trust comes from visible checking, not from silence.
questions.explanation: 新闻编辑室的回答是：信任从来不是靠沉默产生的，看到更正的读者才知道报社在核对。B 项说指控成立并将撤掉栏目，与后文“四年后成为最受欢迎的栏目”相反；A 项说读者根本注意不到，与订阅上升矛盾；D 项说只有对手出错，原文没有这种说法。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: silence 与 checking 的对立

passages.passage:
The bakery begins work at eleven at night, and the initial task given to a new assistant is not baking but cleaning: the tables, the tins, and the floor beneath the ovens, in that order, every night for a fortnight, an order the owner insists is not a form of hazing. Cleaning teaches where everything lives, and a person who has scrubbed the floor knows why flour is kept away from the door. It also reveals, without anyone having to say so, who will still be careful in the third hour of the morning when nobody is watching, which is a question no interview can settle.

By the second week the assistant is allowed to weigh. The recipes are written in percentages rather than grams, so that a batch can be scaled up or down, and this arithmetic is the part most beginners underestimate. A dough that is two per cent too wet will look perfectly fine and taste wrong, and the mistake will not show until the following day, by which point forty loaves have been sold.

The night shift has a discipline of its own. Dough is proved according to the warmth of the room rather than the clock, so the timetable is rewritten every few hours, and the person who has just learned the schedule is the one who must change it.

The owner keeps a notebook of every batch that failed, with the temperature, the timing and the reason, and she reads it before she trains anyone new. Bread is an agricultural product before it is anything else, and the weather in the field decides how much water the flour will take. What she will not do is put a beginner on the ovens before the sixth month. Bread is evaluated by sound as much as by sight, and the sound of a baked loaf is something that can only be learned by standing beside someone who already knows it.

The assistant who stayed longest describes the work differently from the way the owner does. She says the night is not about bread at all; it is about becoming responsible for something that will be judged by strangers in the morning, which she offers as a fair description of most work and a better one than the advertisements give.

questions.stem: What is a new assistant's first task?
options: Cleaning the tables, tins and floor.
Weighing the flour for the first batch.
questions.answer: Cleaning the tables, tins and floor.
questions.explanation: 原文直接点明第一件差事不是烘焙而是清洁三处地方。C 项称重是第二周才允许做的；B 项烤最简单的面包、D 项接顾客订单，原文都没有安排给新人。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why does the owner insist on cleaning for a fortnight?
options: It shows where things belong and who stays careful unobserved.
It saves the cost of hiring extra staff.
It teaches the assistant to bake faster.
It is required by food safety law.
questions.answer: It shows where things belong and who stays careful unobserved.
questions.explanation: 原文给出两层理由：知道东西放在哪，以及在无人看管时谁仍然细致。B 项节省用工成本、D 项食品安全法、C 项学会更快烘焙，原文都没有提到，C 项更与“先清洁后称重”的顺序相反。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why are the recipes written in percentages rather than grams?
options: To make the arithmetic easier for beginners.
To allow the size of a batch to be changed.
questions.answer: To allow the size of a batch to be changed.
questions.explanation: 原文用 so that 说明目的是让一批面团可以放大或缩小。A 项说让算术更容易，原文恰恰说初学者最容易低估这部分算术；B 项说买面粉更便宜、C 项说保密配方，原文均无依据。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: It lists the tools used in a bakery.
It explains why the shift's timetable keeps changing.
It compares day and night wages.
It argues that clocks are unreliable.
questions.answer: It explains why the shift's timetable keeps changing.
questions.explanation: 该段说明发酵看室温而不是看钟点，所以时间表每隔几小时就要重写，功能是解释夜间工序为何不断调整。A 项列举工具、C 项比较日夜工资、D 项论证钟表不可靠，都不是该段做的事。因此答案是 A。

passages.passage:
A coach who has trained distance runners for thirty years says the most common mistake among beginners is measuring training in kilometres. The body, he argues, does not know distance; it knows time and effort, and the two are not the same thing on a windy day or a hilly one.

His method is simple to describe and hard to follow. A runner is told to run for forty minutes at a pace at which conversation remains possible, and to ignore the distance completed entirely. Some runners cover nine kilometres in that time, others six, and both are doing the same session, which is the point the coach repeats until it becomes boring.

The reason for the rule is that the nervous runner will always run faster than instructed, and the confident one will always run further. A watch that measures only time removes both temptations, and it also removes the comparison with a training partner who happens to be taller.

Where the method becomes interesting is in its second year. Runners who trained by time for twelve months were found to have suffered fewer injuries than a group who trained by distance, although the two groups had run for a similar number of hours. The difference was in the last twenty minutes of each session, when the distance-trained group, tired and close to home, tended to push harder than their bodies were ready for.

The coach is careful not to claim too much, and he has refused three offers to sell the method as a course. Time-based training does not make anyone faster than talent or age allows, and it does nothing for the runner who simply prefers the numbers. What it does is make a habit survive the weeks when progress is invisible, which is most weeks.

What he asks of the runners he trains is not discipline but honesty, and he says the two are confused more often than any other pair of words in sport. If the pace makes conversation impossible, the session is too fast, whatever the watch says; if it feels easy for the whole forty minutes, the runner has learned something that no schedule can teach, and that a watch cannot measure.

questions.stem: What is the coach's objection to measuring training in kilometres?
options: The body responds to time and effort, not distance.
Beginners cannot read a watch while running.
Kilometres are difficult to measure accurately.
Distance training is only for professional runners.
questions.answer: The body responds to time and effort, not distance.
questions.explanation: 原文用分号把两层意思并列：身体不认识距离，只认识时间和用力程度。C 项说公里难以准确测量、B 项说新手边跑边看表不方便、D 项说只有专业选手才按距离训练，原文都没有提出。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：分号并列结构

questions.stem: Why does the coach order runners to ignore distance?
options: Because partners cannot agree on a route.
Because runners tend to push harder when a distance is visible.
Because shorter runs are always safer.
Because distance is not recorded by most watches.
questions.answer: Because runners tend to push harder when a distance is visible.
questions.explanation: 原文说紧张的人会跑快，自信的人会跑远，可见问题是“看得见数字就会加码”，屏蔽距离正是为消除这种倾向。D 项说多数手表不记距离、C 项说短跑总更安全、A 项说同伴选不出路线，原文都没有支持。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To compare two coaches in different countries.
To describe the route of a typical session.
To report a comparison that supports the method.
To explain how injuries are treated.
questions.answer: To report a comparison that supports the method.
questions.explanation: 该段以一年后的对照结果为核心：按时间训练的一组受伤更少，总小时数却相近，功能是用证据支持方法本身。D 项说如何治疗伤病、A 项说比较两国教练、B 项说描述路线，都不是该段做的事，其中 A 项尤其原文只提到一位教练。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：证据段的作用

questions.stem: What does the coach consider more valuable than discipline?
options: Strict adherence to a weekly plan.
Honest reading of how the session actually felt.
questions.answer: Honest reading of how the session actually felt.
questions.explanation: 末段直接说他要的不是自律而是诚实，并给出两条判断：说话说不了就是太快，四十分钟都轻松就是学到了东西。C 项说严格遵守周计划、B 项说买更准的表、A 项说跟更快的同伴跑，原文要么没提，要么正是他用来消除的诱惑。因此答案是 A。

passages.passage:
A mill that supplies flour to a hundred bakeries reduced the salt in its standard blend by five per cent a year for six years, and almost nobody noticed. That is the finding the mill's technical director likes best, because the alternative, a single cut of a third, had already been tried in another country and had produced a public argument that lasted a decade.

The arithmetic behind the gradual approach is dull and effective. Salt is cheap but powerful: a change of one per cent in a loaf is invisible in taste tests and measurable in blood pressure studies, and the effect of the change accumulates in the people who eat the bread every morning rather than in the occasional customer.

There were two conditions attached. The first was that the mill would never describe the change as a health measure, since a label announcing a benefit invites a comparison that no baker wants. The second was that the cut would stop if bakers began adding salt themselves, which some of them did, quietly, for about eighteen months.

What made the second condition work was not enforcement but information, which is an uncomfortable finding for anyone who prefers rules. The mill published the salt content of every blend on its invoices, in small print, next to the price. Bakers who added salt did so knowing the number, and most of them stopped once they saw what they were undoing.

Nutritionists who were not involved are divided about the ethics of the method. One view is that it is a form of choice architecture: nobody is deceived, and the default simply moved. The other is that a change too small to notice is a change too small to consent to, and that a customer has a right to know what was done on his behalf.

The technical director does not defend the method in those terms. He points out that the mill has published the figures for six years, that any baker could have asked, and that the alternative was a decade of public argument and no change at all in a single loaf.

questions.stem: Why does the director prefer gradual reductions to one large cut?
options: Salt becomes harmless when reduced slowly.
Gradual changes cost less money for the mill.
Bakers refused to accept any single change.
A sudden large cut had already caused a long public dispute elsewhere.
questions.answer: A sudden large cut had already caused a long public dispute elsewhere.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说一次削减三分之一的做法在另一国试过，引发了持续十年的公开争论，这正是他选渐进的理由。B 项说成本更低，原文说盐便宜；C 项说面包师拒绝任何一次性改动，原文没这么说；A 项说慢慢减盐就无害，原文谈的是血压研究而非无害化。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why was the first condition attached to the plan?
options: Because the mill wanted to raise its prices.
Because a stated health benefit invites the wrong comparison.
Because salt is cheaper than flour.
questions.answer: Because a stated health benefit invites the wrong comparison.
questions.explanation: 原文用 since 说明理由：宣称有好处会让这块面包被拿去和别人比较，而面包师并不愿这样。A 项说磨坊想涨价、D 项说盐比面粉便宜、B 项说面包师不爱读标签，原文都没有支持，其中 D 项只在“盐便宜”这一句出现过，与本题理由无关。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：条件背后的动机

questions.stem: Why did most bakers stop adding salt of their own?
options: They could see on the invoice how much they were undoing.
A new law forbade them to add salt.
The mill stopped selling to them.
Their customers complained about the taste.
questions.answer: They could see on the invoice how much they were undoing.
questions.explanation: 原文说明起作用的是信息而非强制：发票小字印着含盐量，多数人看到自己在抵消什么就停手了。B 项说新法禁止、D 项说顾客抱怨口味、C 项说磨坊停止供货，原文都没有提到，C 项更与“磨坊继续供货”矛盾。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To present the two sides of the ethical argument about the method.
To explain why salt is added to bread.
To describe how flour is milled.
To prove that the mill acted illegally.
questions.answer: To present the two sides of the ethical argument about the method.
questions.explanation: 该段先点明营养学界对做法是否道德存在分歧，再并列两种看法，功能是呈现争议双方。D 项说证明磨坊违法，原文没有法律判断；C 项说描述磨粉工艺、B 项说解释为何加盐，都不是该段内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: One view... The other 结构

passages.passage:
For eleven years the town of Albersdorf advertised itself on roadside boards, in railway carriages, and once, memorably, on the side of a bus that never left the depot. The campaign cost more than the town's library, and the number of visitors rose by a figure that nobody could separate from the general rise in weekend travel.

Then the council stopped. The budget was not reallocated to anything; it was simply not renewed, and for two years the town did nothing to attract anyone. What happened next is the part the tourism office finds hard to explain to its members.

Visitor numbers fell by four per cent in the first year and then rose, slowly, for the next three, until they passed the level the campaign had reached, which took everyone by surprise, the council included. The visitors who came were different: they stayed longer, spent less per day, and were far more likely to say they had heard about the town from a friend.

The explanation the council's own researcher offers is that advertising had been answering a question nobody was asking, and that the town had confused visibility with appeal. A board beside a motorway can tell a driver that a town exists, but it cannot tell him why he should stop, and the people who did stop tended to leave after ninety minutes because there was nothing to keep them.

What the town did instead was quieter. It repaired the path along the river, opened the old mill on Sundays, and allowed the market to spread into two neighbouring streets. None of these was announced; each was simply available, and each gave a visitor a reason to stay until the afternoon, which is more than any board had managed.

The tourism officer, who was against the cut, now describes the result as luck with a lesson in it. The lesson, as she puts it, is that a place is not a product to be pushed but a place, and that the work of making it worth a journey cannot be done by a poster, a fact the town discovered only after it had spent the money.

questions.stem: What happened to visitor numbers when the advertising stopped?
options: They doubled in the first year.
They fell briefly, then rose above the old level.
questions.answer: They fell briefly, then rose above the old level.
questions.explanation: 原文给出先降百分之四、随后三年上升并超过宣传期的水平。C 项说跌下去再没恢复、B 项说完全不变、A 项说第一年翻倍，都与这一描述矛盾。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To explain why the campaign was expensive.
To list the roads that lead into the town.
To compare the town with a neighbouring village.
To show that the kind of visitor changed, not only the number.
questions.answer: To show that the kind of visitor changed, not only the number.
questions.explanation: 该段用 different 一词并列出三项变化，功能是说明游客的构成而非数量。C 项说与邻村比较、B 项说列举进镇道路、A 项说解释宣传为何昂贵，都不是该段内容，其中 A 项属第一段。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：转折段的重点

questions.stem: Why had advertising been ineffective?
options: It cost more than the town could afford.
It attracted the wrong kind of visitor.
It was placed in the wrong railway carriages.
It told drivers the town existed but gave no reason to stay.
questions.answer: It told drivers the town existed but gave no reason to stay.
questions.explanation: 研究者说广告只能告诉司机“有个镇子”，却说不清“为什么停”，停了的人也九十分钟就走。C 项说广告投放在了错误的列车车厢，那只是原文顺带提到的投放地点之一；A 项说花费超出承受能力，原文只说比图书馆贵；B 项说吸引来错误的游客，原文说的是游客停留短。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：手段与目的错配

questions.stem: What is the tourism officer's view of the outcome?
options: It was a mistake that should be reversed.
It shows that visitors prefer cheaper towns.
It proves that all advertising is a waste of money.
It was luck, but it carries a lesson about what a place is.
questions.answer: It was luck, but it carries a lesson about what a place is.
questions.explanation: 原文说她把这个结果称为“带着教训的运气”，教训是地方不是要靠海报推销的产品。C 项说证明一切广告都是浪费，那是绝对化推断，原文没有这样讲；B 项说游客偏好便宜的小镇、A 项说这是该撤回的错误，都与她的评价不符。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: luck with a lesson 的含义

passages.passage:
Ask an adult how a bicycle pump works and most will answer with confidence; ask the same adult to draw one and the confidence collapses. Psychologists call this the illusion of explanatory depth, and it is more common than the name suggests.

In a series of studies volunteers rated their understanding of a familiar device, then explained it in writing, then rated it again. The average rating fell by nearly half between the first and the third question, and the fall was steepest for the volunteers who had been most certain at the start. The pattern held when the device was replaced by a familiar public institution, which the team had not expected.

The effect is not confined to objects. It appears when people rate their understanding of political policies, of medical treatments and of the tax system, and it appears in the same shape every time: high confidence, a request for detail, a quiet correction.

What makes the finding useful rather than merely amusing is what happens afterwards. Volunteers who had been asked to explain something became, in later questions, noticeably more willing to say that they did not know, and less willing to accept a simple solution offered by a stranger, and slower to change their minds afterwards.

The researchers are cautious about the size of this effect. One experiment is not a cure for overconfidence, and the participants were students in a laboratory rather than voters at a polling station. What the experiment does show is that a single request for detail is enough to move a rating, which is a modest claim and a portable one. It travels: the same exercise is now used in training engineers, who must explain a bridge before they are allowed to inspect one.

It also suggests something about interviews and examinations. The cheapest way to test whether someone understands a subject may not be to ask whether they do, but to ask them to explain it to a person who does not, and to listen for the moment when the explanation turns into a list of terms. That moment, the researchers note, is usually audible.

questions.stem: What happens to confidence when people are asked to explain a device?
options: It drops sharply, most of all among the most confident.
It stays the same until the end of the study.
It falls only among the least confident.
It rises because the question is easier.
questions.answer: It drops sharply, most of all among the most confident.
questions.explanation: 原文明确指出平均评分几乎下降一半，且降幅以最自信的那组最大。B 项说保持不变、D 项说因为问题更容易而上升、C 项说只有最不自信的人下降，都与“降幅最大者最自信”这一句相反。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the illusion of explanatory depth?
options: Forgetting facts soon after learning them.
Feeling sure you understand something until you must explain it.
Believing that all machines work in the same way.
questions.answer: Feeling sure you understand something until you must explain it.
questions.explanation: 第一段用打气筒的例子给出定义：能自信作答，却画不出来，即“自信于理解，直到要解释”。C 项说认为所有机器原理相同、A 项说学过就忘、D 项说偏爱图而非文字，原文都没有定义这层意思。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To explain how the studies were funded.
To argue that confidence cannot be measured.
To compare two groups of researchers.
To describe a lasting change in behaviour after the exercise.
questions.answer: To describe a lasting change in behaviour after the exercise.
questions.explanation: 该段以 afterwards 开头，报告的是解释练习之后的行为变化：更愿意承认不知道、更不愿接受陌生人给的简单方案，功能是说明效果的延续。C 项比较两组研究者、A 项说经费来源、B 项说自信无法测量，都不是该段内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：后续效应的表述

questions.stem: What do the researchers warn against?
options: Using bicycles as examples in research.
Treating one laboratory result as a cure for overconfidence.
Publishing results before they are checked.
questions.answer: Treating one laboratory result as a cure for overconfidence.
questions.explanation: 原文用 not a cure 与 students in a laboratory rather than voters at a polling station 两处限定，说明他们在意的是不要把单一实验结果当成普遍解决方案。A 项说不要用自行车举例，那只是开头的例证；C 项说不要让学生写解释，那正是实验做法；D 项说不要提前发表，原文未提。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：限定语的分量

passages.passage:
A district that moved its secondary school start from eight o'clock to half past eight reported, after two years, a rise in attendance and a fall in the number of pupils sent home for sleeping in class. The change cost almost nothing, which is why other districts have found it hard to explain their own reluctance.

The argument rests on a fact about adolescence that has been known for thirty years and ignored for most of them. At puberty the internal clock shifts, and a sixteen-year-old who is asked to sleep at eleven and wake at six is being asked to do something his body cannot easily do. The shift is not a preference, and it cannot be corrected by discipline; it can only be accommodated.

The objections are practical rather than scientific, and they are serious. Buses, sports fixtures, part-time jobs and the school day of younger siblings are all arranged around the earlier start, and a change in one school moves four timetables at once.

The district's solution was to move everything in a single year and to accept a year of complaints. Sports fixtures were moved to the afternoon, the bus contract was rewritten at a small extra cost, and the primary schools started fifteen minutes later than before, which turned out to be the part parents minded least. The bus company, which had opposed the change, now runs the same routes an hour later and reports fuller vehicles.

What the district did not do was explain the science first. The superintendent says the opposite order worked better: families accepted the new timetable because the buses ran and the fixtures happened, and the explanation came afterwards, in a letter that most of them read and few of them answered.

Not every problem yielded. Pupils who work before school still work before school, and the district has added nothing for them. The gain in attendance, the superintendent says, is real and uneven, and it is the unevenness that a district has to be honest about when it reports to the board, and the board has asked for a third year of figures.

questions.stem: What two changes did the district report after two years?
options: Attendance rose and fewer pupils were sent home.
Shorter lessons and a later finish.
More sports fixtures and a larger bus fleet.
Higher exam marks and fewer teachers leaving.
questions.answer: Attendance rose and fewer pupils were sent home.
questions.explanation: 原文明确列出两项结果：出勤率上升、因上课睡觉被送回家的学生减少。D 项说成绩提高与教师流失减少、B 项说课时缩短与放学更晚、C 项说赛事更多与车队更大，原文都没有作为结果给出。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：结果的并列项
rise 与 fall 的对应

questions.stem: What is the objection the district faced?
options: Parents refused to read the letters.
The scientific evidence was too weak.
Four timetables depended on the early start.
questions.answer: Four timetables depended on the early start.
questions.explanation: 原文说反对意见是“现实的而非科学的”，并点明校车、赛事、兼职与弟妹的作息都围绕早读安排，改一所学校就牵动四张时间表。B 项说科学证据太弱，与“反对是现实考量”相反；A 项说家长不看信、D 项说高年级学生反对，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：反对意见的性质

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To explain why pupils work before school.
To argue that the practical arrangements mattered more than the explanation.
To describe the content of the superintendent's letter.
To compare two districts' bus contracts.
questions.answer: To argue that the practical arrangements mattered more than the explanation.
questions.explanation: 该段说明先做事、后解释的顺序更有效，理由是校车开了、赛事办了，家长就接受了，功能是论证“安排胜过说明”。C 项只说信的内容、D 项比较两份校车合同、A 项解释学生为何课前打工，都不是该段重点，其中 A 项属末段。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What does the superintendent insist on mentioning in her report?
options: That the gain was uneven across pupils.
That the change cost a great deal.
That other districts should copy the plan.
That pupils who work have been helped.
questions.answer: That the gain was uneven across pupils.
questions.explanation: 末段两次提到 unevenness，并说这正是向董事会汇报时必须如实说明的部分。B 项说改动花费巨大，与“几乎没花钱”相反；D 项说课前打工的学生得到了帮助，原文恰恰说“没有为他们做任何事”；C 项说其他学区应当照搬，原文没这个主张。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：作者强调的重点

passages.passage:
A company that builds face-recognition tools has been training its models on photographs taken from public profiles, and until last year it said so only in the eleventh paragraph of a privacy notice.

The photographs were not secret. They had been posted, usually by their subjects, usually in order to be seen. What the company did with them was different in kind from what the posters had done: it turned a picture of a person into a measurement of a face, and then sold the measurement onward. A measurement can be stored, compared and combined with other measurements, and none of that was true of the photograph itself.

Two arguments are made in the company's defence, and both deserve to be stated properly. The first is that the pictures were public, and that a public picture is not a private one. The second is that the tool is used to find missing children, which is true, and which does not describe most of its customers.

The regulators who examined the case accepted neither argument as complete. Public availability, they wrote, is a fact about access rather than a permission for use, and a photograph posted to show a new haircut carries no consent to be measured. They added that a use justified by its best customer is a use that has not been justified at all.

What has changed since is smaller than the headlines implied. The company now asks permission where it can identify the person, removes pictures on request, and publishes the list of datasets it uses. None of this repairs the pictures taken before 2022; it only prevents some of the next ones. The company also says it has stopped selling to two categories of customer that it declines to name.

The chief executive, who kept his job, describes the episode as a lesson about consent that the industry learned late. Critics point out that the lesson was learned after the profits were counted, and that the people in the photographs were never asked, which is the part that no policy can undo. The regulators have opened a second inquiry, which is expected to report next year.

questions.stem: How did the company describe its use of the photographs?
options: On the front page of its website.
So deep in its privacy notice that few readers would find it.
In a press release about missing children.
In a letter to the regulators.
questions.answer: So deep in its privacy notice that few readers would find it.
questions.explanation: 原文说它直到去年才在隐私声明的第十一段里提到这件事，即披露位置极其靠后。C 项说在关于失踪儿童的新闻稿里、A 项说在网站首页、D 项说在给监管机构的信里，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What made the company's use different in kind from the posters' use?
options: It kept the pictures for longer than a year.
It converted pictures into measurements that could be sold.
It paid the people in the pictures.
It posted the pictures in more places.
questions.answer: It converted pictures into measurements that could be sold.
questions.explanation: 原文把差别定为“性质不同”：把人的照片变成面部的测量结果，再把测量结果卖出去。D 项说发布到更多地方、C 项说给照片里的人付钱、A 项说保存超过一年，原文都没有提，其中 C 项与“从未征得同意”相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：用途性质的差别

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To reject both defences and state the regulators' reasoning.
To list the datasets the company uses.
To explain how recognition tools are built.
questions.answer: To reject both defences and state the regulators' reasoning.
questions.explanation: 该段开头即说两个理由都不被接受，随后用两句给出监管方的理由（可获取不等于可使用、以备用的用途不等于已获正当性），功能是驳回并为驳回提供论证。C 项列举数据集属末段、D 项讲技术原理、B 项比较两份报告，都不是该段内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：驳论段的构成

questions.stem: What is the critics' complaint about the chief executive's account?
options: He refused to publish the list of datasets.
He blamed his employees for the decision.
The lesson came after the profit, and the people were never asked.
questions.answer: The lesson came after the profit, and the people were never asked.
questions.explanation: 原文说批评者指出教训是在算完利润之后才学到的，而照片里的人从未被征询意见。A 项说拒绝公布数据集，与“已公布清单”相反；C 项说他立即离职，原文说他还留在职位上；B 项说他把责任推给员工，原文没有。因此答案是 A。

passages.passage:
The bicycle workshop behind the library opens three afternoons a week, and the sixteen people who work in it are apprentices, most of them still at school. They repair bicycles for anyone who brings one, and they charge for parts and nothing else, which is why the queue begins before the door is unlocked.

The scheme started as a way of teaching a trade to pupils who were not thriving in classrooms, and it has quietly become something the town depends on. Two hundred bicycles were repaired last year, the waiting list runs to six weeks in spring, and the local hospital sends its porters' bicycles here rather than to the shop that charges by the hour.

What the apprentices learn first is not repair but diagnosis. A machine arrives with a complaint that is rarely accurate: the owner says the gears slip when the chain is worn, or that the brakes are weak when the wheel is untrue. Learning to listen, then to test, then to disagree politely with a person twice your age takes longer than learning to replace a chain, and the instructor says half of the first year is spent on it.

The workshop's strangest rule is that every repair must be explained to the owner before anyone is paid. Apprentices rehearse this on each other, and the ones who talk too fast are sent back to the bench until the explanation is clear enough for a person who has never seen a derailleur. The rule exists, the instructor says, because a customer who understands a repair returns, and a customer who suspects he has been sold something returns angry.

Not everything works. Three apprentices left last year for jobs that paid more, and the workshop has no answer beyond a reference and a good word. One bicycle was ruined by a mistake nobody noticed until its owner rode it away and came back two streets later.

The instructor nevertheless measures success in a way a school would find odd: he counts how many apprentices argue with him about a diagnosis, and last year the number was eleven, the highest the workshop has recorded.

questions.stem: What do customers pay for at the workshop?
questions.explanation: 原文说只收零件费、其余分文不取。D 项说只收工费、B 项说两者都收、A 项说全由镇里出钱，都与这一句直接冲突。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: What does the workshop mainly teach in its first year?
options: How to replace a worn chain quickly.
How to deal with angry customers.
How to price a repair fairly.
How to work out what is actually wrong.
questions.answer: How to work out what is actually wrong.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说第一年学的不是修理而是“诊断”，并解释顾客的描述常常不准，故重点在于查明真正的问题。A 项说快速换链条，原文恰恰说这比诊断容易；C 项说定价、B 项说应付愤怒顾客，都不是第一年的教学内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 主旨理解：重点句的否定结构

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fourth paragraph?
options: To give the reason behind the explain-before-payment rule.
To list the tools the workshop owns.
To compare two kinds of bicycle.
To describe how apprentices are paid.
questions.answer: To give the reason behind the explain-before-payment rule.
questions.explanation: 该段先讲规则内容，再用 because 给出理由：懂了的顾客会回来，怀疑被推销的顾客会生气地回来，功能是为规则提供依据。D 项说学徒如何领薪、C 项比较两种自行车、B 项列举工具，都不是该段任务。因此答案是 A。

questions.stem: Why does the instructor count arguments?
options: Because arguments shorten the waiting list.
Because the school requires a record of conflict.
Because disagreement shows an apprentice can judge for himself.
questions.answer: Because disagreement shows an apprentice can judge for himself.
questions.explanation: 末段把这句当作“成功”的衡量方式，说明他要的是能独立判断的学徒，而不是照单执行的人。A 项说争吵能缩短等候名单、C 项说他不喜欢听话的学徒（过于绝对）、B 项说学校要求记录冲突，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：成功标准的选择

passages.passage:
In a village where only four hundred people live there is a handwritten chronicle that has been kept, without a break, for two hundred years. It records births, deaths, harvests, the price of salt and, occasionally, a quarrel that lasted three generations.

The book lives in a wooden box in the house of the family that began it, and the sixth keeper is a woman of thirty-four who teaches mathematics in a town nearby. She writes for an hour on Sunday evenings, in a hand that deliberately imitates her great-grandmother's, and she says the imitation is a way of not being the last.

Historians who have examined the volumes value them for what they record by accident: the weather in years when nobody wrote anything else, the names of labourers who appear in no other document, the prices that show when a road reached the village and when the railway did not. The box itself is plain, and its lock has been replaced four times without ever being forced.

The keeper knows this and will not sell. Two universities have offered to digitise the whole chronicle and return the box, and she has accepted the scanning and refused the removal, on the ground that a record kept in one place is a record that belongs to that place. A copy in a city, she says, is a copy; the book in the box is the village's memory, and memory that leaves home stops being memory and becomes evidence.

What she worries about is not theft but habit. Her daughter is eleven and has written three entries; her son is nineteen and has written none, and says the chronicle is a hobby of their mother's. The keeper concedes that the seventh keeper may close the sequence, and that two hundred years would then be a finished book rather than a broken one, which is the sort of distinction only a keeper would make.

She has therefore begun teaching the village's children to read the old hand, four at a time, in the school holidays. It is slow, it may fail, and it is the only plan she has.

questions.stem: What does the chronicle contain besides births and deaths?
questions.explanation: 原文逐一列出：出生、死亡、收成、盐价，偶尔还有延续三代人的争吵。C 项说田地地图、D 项说官方信件抄本、A 项说食谱与药方，原文都没有提到。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：并列项的完整提取

questions.stem: Why does the keeper refuse to let the box leave the village?
options: She believes the box is worth a fortune.
She thinks a record's value depends on staying where it was written.
She wants a higher price from the universities.
questions.answer: She thinks a record's value depends on staying where it was written.
questions.explanation: 原文给出她的理由：留在原地的记录属于那个地方，离开家的记忆就变成“证据”而不是记忆。D 项说想抬价，原文明确接受扫描、拒绝搬走，与钱无关；B 项说她不信扫描设备，与“接受扫描”矛盾；A 项说箱子很值钱，原文未提。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：比喻背后的立场
evidence 与 memory 的对比

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To compare a daughter and a son.
To describe the real risk, which is a lack of future keepers.
To explain how the chronicle is bound.
questions.answer: To describe the real risk, which is a lack of future keepers.
questions.explanation: 该段用 not theft but habit 转折，把风险从被盗转到“没人继续写”，并落到“第七位记录者可能终结这条线”。D 项讲装订、A 项只是用来举例说明习惯的断裂、C 项讲史学家的批评，都不是该段主旨。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：转折句确立重点

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the keeper's teaching plan?
options: It is funded by the two universities.
It is an uncertain attempt to keep the practice alive.
It has already attracted a hundred children.
It replaces the chronicle with lessons.
questions.answer: It is an uncertain attempt to keep the practice alive.
questions.explanation: 末句三个分句连用：慢、可能失败、却是唯一的办法，说明这是一次没有把握的延续尝试。C 项说已吸引上百孩子，原文只提四个一批；A 项说由两所大学出资，原文未提；D 项说用课程取代村志，与“继续写下去”的目的相反。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 主旨理解：末句三个分句的合力

passages.passage:
A theatre in the east of the city reopened last spring with a stage that no longer has a front. The audience sits on three sides of the acting area, the back wall has come down, and the actors enter through a corridor that used to be a store room.

The rebuilding cost less than a new lighting rig and has altered almost everything else. Its architects describe the result as an instrument rather than a container, and the phrase has been repeated in every interview since. Actors who spent their careers facing one direction now have to move, and the director says the first month of rehearsals was spent teaching people where to stand and when to turn.

The gain is in what the audience can see: a face turned away from the front is still a face when there is no front, and a whisper that used to be inaudible reaches the third row without amplification. The theatre's own survey found that audiences remembered the plays better, a result the director treats as evidence and the board treats as anecdote.

The costs are real and less photographed. Scene changes that were hidden behind a curtain now happen in full view, and the crew has learned to work in costume; tickets for the cheapest seats, which used to be at the back, are now at the ends, and the people who liked the back have complained.

What the director will not claim is that the new arrangement is better: he says it is different, that some plays want a frame and a distance, and that the theatre will keep one production a year on a conventional stage for exactly that reason, which is the compromise that has kept the board quiet. Whether that is generosity or calculation is a question he declines to answer.

The board has asked for a second year of figures before it decides whether to rebuild the other auditorium, which seats six hundred and has not been touched since 1978. The director says he would rather wait for the figures than argue for the idea, and that if the second year resembles the first he will have the argument anyway.

questions.stem: How has the audience's seating changed?
options: It has been reduced to six hundred seats.
It now faces a newly built back wall.
It now surrounds the stage on three sides.
It has been moved further from the stage.
questions.answer: It now surrounds the stage on three sides.
questions.explanation: 首段直接说明观众坐在表演区的三面，即环绕式。D 项说座位离台更远、A 项说缩减到六百座（那是另一座礼堂）、B 项说面对新修的后墙（后墙已被拆掉），都与原文冲突。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：空间关系的表述
sits on three sides 的含义

questions.stem: What does "anecdote" mean in the fourth paragraph?
options: A plan for the next season.
An unproven story rather than solid proof.
questions.answer: An unproven story rather than solid proof.
questions.explanation: 照应与 evidence 相对：导演当作证据，董事会当作“轶事”，说明董事会认为它只是未经证实的故事。B 项说经过仔细测量的结果，恰恰是 evidence 一侧；D 项说观众投诉，原文的投诉另有所指；A 项说下季计划，与语境无关。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 词义猜测：对照关系定词义
evidence 与 anecdote 的对立

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To describe the lighting rig in detail.
To praise the crew's new costumes.
To admit a limit to the new arrangement.
To explain how tickets are priced.
questions.answer: To admit a limit to the new arrangement.
questions.explanation: 该段以“他不会声称新的安排更好”开头，并说明有些戏需要画框与距离，功能是承认这套安排的局限。A 项讲灯光设备、B 项夸服装、D 项讲票价，都不是该段的任务，其中 D 项属第四段。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：让步段的作用

questions.stem: What does the director expect if the second year repeats the first?
options: He will stop surveying the audience.
He will ask the board to lower ticket prices.
He will abandon the three-sided stage.
He will have the evidence to argue for rebuilding.
questions.answer: He will have the evidence to argue for rebuilding.
questions.explanation: 末段说他宁愿等数据，因为第二年的结果若与第一年相似，他就“自然有了论据”，即可以据此主张改建另一座礼堂。C 项说放弃三面舞台、B 项说要求降价、A 项说停止调查，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：条件句的言外之意

passages.passage:
A study that asked two thousand adults how often they glanced at a phone during a conversation found that the answer was, on average, once every four minutes, and that most of them had estimated once every twenty.

The gap between the behaviour and the estimate is the interesting part. People are poor witnesses of their own attention, and they are poorer still when the attention is divided in a way that feels entirely normal to them.

The researchers then ran an experiment with pairs of strangers. In half the pairs one person was instructed to glance at a phone twice during a ten-minute conversation; in the other half no phone appeared at all. The partners who had been glanced at rated the conversation lower on trust and higher on distraction, and they were markedly less willing to meet again, a result the team reproduced twice before publishing it.

What makes this difficult to use as advice is that the size of the effect depended on the relationship. Between strangers the cost was measurable; between couples who had lived together for years it was smaller, and in a few cases the partner noticed nothing. The researchers are careful not to conclude that long familiarity licenses carelessness, only that it absorbs it, and they note that a couple's tolerance may be the result of years of practice rather than of indifference.

The practical advice the study does offer is narrower than the headlines suggested. It is not "put the phone away" but "say what you are doing": a person who announces that he is checking the time is rated almost as highly as a person who does not check at all, which suggests that the damage is to the sense of being attended to rather than to the conversation itself.

The authors end with a caution that is easy to skip. Self-reports of attention are unreliable, their measures cover a single ten-minute conversation, and a laboratory room is not a kitchen at seven in the evening. They say the finding should be tested in homes before it is repeated in advice columns.

questions.stem: How did the estimate compare with the measured behaviour?
options: People checked their phones far less often than they thought.
People checked their phones far more often than they thought.
People refused to give any estimate at all.
The estimate and the measurement were almost identical.
questions.answer: People checked their phones far more often than they thought.
questions.explanation: 实测每四分钟一次，而多数人估计每二十分钟一次，实测频率远高于自我估计。A 项方向相反；D 项说两者几乎一致，与四分钟对二十分钟的差距冲突；C 项说拒绝估计，首段明确有估计值。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：两组数据的比较

questions.stem: What did the experiment find about partners who were glanced at?
options: They enjoyed the conversation more because it felt casual.
They asked to check their own phones.
Their trust fell and they were reluctant to meet the person again.
They did not notice the phone at all.
questions.answer: Their trust fell and they were reluctant to meet the person again.
questions.explanation: 原文说这些人的信任评分更低、分心评分更高，并明显更不愿再见面，可见对方看手机损害了体验。A 项说因为显得随意而更喜欢、D 项说完全没注意、B 项说也想看手机，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：评分差异的含义

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To review the headlines the study received.
To compare phones with other devices.
To explain how the pairs were selected.
To narrow the advice to announcing what you are doing.
questions.answer: To narrow the advice to announcing what you are doing.
questions.explanation: 该段先否定流行说法，再给出更窄的建议：说明你在做什么，并用评分数据支撑，功能是把结论收窄到可操作的层面。A 项说评论媒体标题，原文只提到标题比结论更宽；B 项比较其他设备、C 项说如何配对，都不是该段内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：从宽泛到可操作

questions.stem: What is the authors' attitude towards applying the finding?
options: Confident, since the sample was large.
Cautious, because the evidence comes from one artificial setting.
Indifferent, because the effect was small.
Hostile towards anyone who uses a phone.
questions.answer: Cautious, because the evidence comes from one artificial setting.
questions.explanation: 末段连用三处限定（自我报告不可靠、只覆盖一次十分钟对话、实验室不是厨房），并主张先在家里验证再写进专栏，可见态度是审慎。A 项说因样本大而自信、C 项说漠不关心、D 项说敌视使用者，都与这种限定语气不符。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：限定语判定立场

passages.passage:
The weekly paper in a town of nine thousand stopped printing the names of people charged with minor offences last January. The editor expected letters of thanks; what he received were letters of complaint, most of them from readers who said the paper had stopped doing its job.

The argument for the change was practical. Court lists arrived on Thursday, the paper went to press on Friday, and the only thing a reporter could reliably add in that time was the name and the charge, which is to say the part that follows a person for years after the case has been dropped.

The argument against it was also practical, and the editor states it himself. A local paper's authority rests on the fact that it goes where nobody else goes: to the magistrates' court, on a Thursday, to write down what happened. Remove the names and the reporting is still there, but the readers who care about it feel that something has been taken out of it.

What the paper does instead is report the case, the outcome and the sentence without the name, unless the offence is serious enough that the public interest plainly outweighs the embarrassment. In the first year that exception was used eleven times out of three hundred and forty cases, and the editor says the eleven are the ones that mattered, which is the sort of claim a reader may reasonably doubt.

The circulation figures are the part nobody predicted. Sales fell by six per cent in the first quarter, then recovered, then rose slightly above where they had been, and the editor has no explanation he trusts; his reporters say the court page, which used to be read for names, is now read for what happens next.

He is careful not to claim a principle he cannot defend. He says he does not know whether the change is right, only that the old arrangement was indefensible and the new one is at least arguable, and that a paper which cannot say which of its own decisions it would defend has stopped being useful to anybody.

questions.stem: What did the paper stop printing?
questions.explanation: 首段明确说停止刊出“被控轻微违法者的姓名”。B 项说不再登任何庭审名单，原文说报道仍在；C 项说结果与判决不登，恰恰相反；D 项说不再去治安法庭，原文说这正是它仍在做的事。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：停止对象的界定

questions.stem: Why was the name and charge all a reporter could add?
options: There was almost no time between the list and the deadline.
The court refused to release other details.
questions.answer: There was almost no time between the list and the deadline.
questions.explanation: 原文把“周四拿到名单、周五付印”作为限制条件，说明可核实的信息只剩姓名与罪名。D 项说法院不公开其他细节、B 项说编辑禁止长文、C 项说读者只要姓名，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：时间限制的含义

questions.stem: What is the main function of the third paragraph?
options: To explain how the paper is printed.
To describe the layout of the court.
To state the strongest objection to the change.
questions.answer: To state the strongest objection to the change.
questions.explanation: 该段以“反对的理由同样是现实的”开头，随后说明地方报纸的权威在于“别人不去的地方它去”，功能是替反对者把最强的一击说出来。B 项描述法庭布局、D 项比较两家报纸、A 项讲印刷流程，都不是该段内容。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：对立论证的呈现

questions.stem: What is the editor's attitude towards his own decision?
options: He regrets it and plans to restore the names.
He treats it as arguable rather than certainly right.
He is certain it was the only defensible choice.
He believes readers will forget within a year.
questions.answer: He treats it as arguable rather than certainly right.
questions.explanation: 末段明说他不知道改动是否正确，只知道旧做法站不住脚、新做法至少可辩，可见态度是“可辩而非确定”。C 项说确信是唯一定法，与“不知道是否正确”矛盾；A 项说后悔并打算恢复，原文未提；D 项说读者一年内会忘，属无关推断。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：限定表达判定立场

passages.passage:
A city that set out to plant ten thousand trees in three years finished with nine thousand and a map that shows, street by street, where those nine thousand do the least good. The map was not part of the plan; it was made afterwards by a summer student, from a satellite record of surface temperature.

The map found that the trees planted in the wealthiest streets cooled them by almost nothing, because those streets already possessed mature trees and a canopy that keeps the ground shaded. The trees planted in the poorest streets, where there had been none, cooled them by up to four degrees, and the difference was not the species or the dimensions of the sapling but what was already standing there.

The lesson would be unremarkable if planting had been planned with it in mind. It was not: the city planted where residents asked, and residents with gardens and time ask more often than residents working two jobs, so the programme had, unintentionally, spent the majority of its money on the streets that needed it least.

The correction now in place is a rule that a third of each year's planting goes to the twelve postcodes with the highest summer temperatures and the lowest tree cover, which is an admittedly clumsy instrument and, the officer in charge admits, the first instrument that has ever directed the money at the heat.

There is a cost to the rule that the officer does not disguise. Planting in those streets is considerably slower: the ground is harder, the residents are less able to water young trees, and two of the initial four sites lost approximately half their saplings in the first summer. The municipality has begun paying residents a modest sum to water them, which is a new idea and not yet a policy.

What the map has changed, in the end, is the question the city asks. It used to ask how many trees had been planted and now asks where they were planted, which is a harder question to answer in a press release and a considerably better one to answer during a heatwave.

questions.stem: What did the map show about the trees in the wealthiest streets?
options: They grew faster than trees elsewhere.
They cost twice as much as expected.
They were the only trees that survived.
They cooled those streets hardly at all.
questions.answer: They cooled those streets hardly at all.
questions.explanation: 原文说富裕街区新栽的树几乎没带来降温，因为那里本来就有成熟树冠。A 项说长得更快、B 项说成本翻倍、C 项说只有它们存活，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 细节理解：程度副词的限制

questions.stem: Why did most of the money go to streets that needed it least?
options: Planting followed requests, and those residents asked more often.
Contracts required planting in wealthy areas.
The city's maps were drawn by wealthier districts.
Poorer streets had soil that could not hold trees.
questions.answer: Planting followed requests, and those residents asked more often.
questions.explanation: 原文把原因归于“按申请种树”，而有庭院与空闲的居民更常提出申请，于是资源自然偏向本不缺树的街区。C 项说地图由富裕区绘制、D 项说穷人街区土壤不适合、B 项说合同有此要求，原文都没有。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：制度性偏向的成因

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To praise the residents for watering.
To compare two kinds of sapling.
To explain how satellites measure heat.
To admit what the new rule costs in practice.
questions.answer: To admit what the new rule costs in practice.
questions.explanation: 该段开门见山承认新规有代价，随后列出地面坚硬、居民无力浇水、四个点死了半数树苗，功能是如实交代实施代价。B 项比较树种、C 项讲卫星测温、A 项称赞居民浇水，都不是该段的重点，其中 A 项只是应对办法。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：让步段与代价陈述

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why cities should plant ten thousand trees.
Why wealthy residents oppose new trees.
How satellites are used to plan parks.
How a map redirected where the city planted its trees.
questions.answer: How a map redirected where the city planted its trees.
questions.explanation: 全文线索是：种树完成—地图揭示分布偏差—规则改为按高温与树冠分配—代价—问题从“种了多少”变成“种在哪里”，核心是地图如何改变种树地点。C 项只涉方法、A 项是口号、B 项原文未提富裕居民反对。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 主旨理解：结构线索的收束

passages.passage:
A workshop in the north of the country repairs washing machines that their manufacturer stopped making in 2004, and it does so with parts that the manufacturer no longer sells, taken from machines its customers no longer want.

The workshop is legal, and it is legal because of a rule few people know exists: a manufacturer must supply spare parts for a stated number of years, and after that period anyone may copy them, provided the copy is not sold as if it were the original. The workshop copies them in a small room at the back and sells them at a third of the price the manufacturer used to charge, which is the gap the manufacturer has twice tried to close.

The first attempt was an argument that the copies were unsafe; a court found that they were not. The second was an argument that the copies infringed a design right; a court found that a design right does not cover a part whose only purpose is to fit a machine that its maker has abandoned.

What the workshop sells most of, however, is not parts but time. A machine that is repaired lasts four years longer than one that is replaced, and the workshop's own figures, which nobody outside has checked, suggest that it has kept eleven thousand machines out of the waste stream since 2011.

The uncomfortable part is who pays. The manufacturer loses a sale, the customer saves two hundred pounds, and the cost of the extra four years falls on an electricity bill and on nobody else, which the owner says is the whole argument and would be easier to make if his own margins were not so comfortable.

Regulators are drafting a rule that would extend the period during which parts must be supplied, from ten years to fifteen, and the manufacturer's lobby is resisting it with the argument that longer periods make machines more expensive to design, which is an argument about price rather than about waste. The owner has been asked to speak at the hearing and has agreed, on condition that he may bring a machine that still works.

questions.stem: Why did the manufacturer's second legal argument fail?
options: A design claim cannot cover a part made for an abandoned machine.
The workshop had bought the design right.
The copies were shown to be unsafe after all.
The court refused to hear the argument.
questions.answer: A design claim cannot cover a part made for an abandoned machine.
questions.explanation: 原文引述判决理由：外观设计权不覆盖“唯一用途是装到已被弃用机器上”的零件，因此该主张不成立。C 项说副本被证明确实不安全，与第一次诉讼的结论相反；B 项说工坊买下了设计权，原文未提；D 项说法院拒绝受理，与“法院作出认定”矛盾。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 推理判断：判决理由的适用范围

questions.stem: What does "the gap" refer to in the second paragraph?
options: A physical space at the back of the workshop.
The difference between two machine models.
The period between two court cases.
The market the copies have taken from the manufacturer.
questions.answer: The market the copies have taken from the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: “缺口”指工坊以三分之一价格出售复制零件，抢走了原厂的市场，因而原厂两次想“堵上”。A 项指工坊后屋的实体空间，那是 copiing 的地方而非 gap；C 项指两次诉讼之间的时间、B 项指两种机型的差别，都与“两次试图堵上”的语境不合。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 词义猜测：上下文界定抽象名词

questions.stem: What is the main function of the fifth paragraph?
options: To show where the burden of the extra years falls.
To explain how washing machines are assembled.
questions.answer: To show where the burden of the extra years falls.
questions.explanation: 该段以“不舒服的地方在于谁付钱”开头，逐项分配得失：原厂少卖一台、顾客省两百镑、多出的四年落在电费上，功能是交代成本归属。B 项讲装配流程、D 项比较电价、C 项批评店主利润，都不是该段主体，其中 C 项只是末句的自我限定。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 语篇功能：成本分配的陈述

questions.stem: Why does the owner want to bring a working machine to the hearing?
options: To show the committee that repair keeps machines in use.
To prove that copies are cheaper than parts.
To sell the machine to the regulators.
To demonstrate that the design right is invalid.
questions.answer: To show the committee that repair keeps machines in use.
questions.explanation: 他要带一台仍在运转的旧机器到场，用实物证明“修得好的机器还在服役”，从而支持延长零件供应期的主张。C 项说卖给监管者、B 项说证明复制件更便宜（原文说价格是原厂三分之一，但这不是他要证明的重点）、D 项说证明设计权无效，都不是带机器的目的。因此答案是 A。
knowledge_points: 观点态度：条件句透露的意图

passages.passage:
When a community music group began holding open practice evenings in an old railway hall, its members expected only a few curious neighbours. They also thought a handful of families might wait quietly for the players to finish. Instead, people came with children, notebooks, walking sticks, and questions about instruments they had never tried closely before. The group had lost its usual concert audience during a long period of repairs at the town hall. The open evenings were first planned as a brief answer. They soon became the part of the week that players and residents valued most, because the hall let people listen without needing expert knowledge or costly tickets.

During a normal evening, the conductor explains why a passage is repeated, and a violin player shows how bow pressure changes the sound. Members of the audience are also invited to move closer when the music becomes quiet. These comments do not turn the event into a lecture; rather, they make the small decisions of a performance visible and give listeners a reason to care about details they might otherwise miss. One older resident said that she had attended concerts for decades but had never realised how much silent counting took place before a group began together.

A teenager who came only to finish a school project returned each week and later joined the youth singing group. This showed that access can lead to taking part when the first step is made easy. The third part of the evening is less formal on purpose: chairs are moved, visitors may ask short questions, and the group tries a new piece in front of everyone. This part matters because it changes the audience from judges of a finished product into witnesses of a process that is not yet fixed. Not every test succeeds, and the players sometimes stop after a few bars, laugh, and begin again; those moments make the art feel human rather than distant.

The town hall has now opened again, but the group has decided to keep the open evenings and make them a lasting part of its season. Its experience suggests that arts groups become stronger when they offer people more than a seat at the end of the work, inviting them instead into the questions, mistakes, and discoveries that give a performance meaning.

questions.stem: What central idea does the passage develop about cultural events?
options: Children learn instruments faster when they watch adults.
Audiences benefit when the creative process is opened to them.
Community music depends mainly on public funding.
Music groups should replace formal concerts with open evenings.
questions.answer: Audiences benefit when the creative process is opened to them.
questions.explanation: 全文从观众进入排练现场、理解演奏选择，写到参与者逐渐加入，中心在于开放艺术过程带来的价值。D 项把“保留开放排练”误读为“取消正式音乐会”；C 项夸大了公共资金的作用，A 项把个别青少年的经历扩大为普遍学习规律。主旨题需要概括全文变化，而不是抓住单一细节。

questions.stem: Why did the group decide to keep the open evenings after the town hall opened again?
options: The format had created a strong connection with the community.
The town council required every concert to be free.
The musicians wanted to avoid performing finished works.
The music group could no longer afford the town hall.
questions.answer: The format had created a strong connection with the community.

passages.passage:
On the first Saturday of every month, the community centre opens its main room to a repair club where neighbours bring damaged lamps, coats, loose chair legs, and small machines that have stopped working. No money changes hands, and no one is expected to know how to repair anything before arriving. Instead, volunteers sit beside visitors, explain each step, and invite the owner to hold the tool or test the switch.

The aim is not simply to rescue an object but to reduce waste while helping people understand how everyday products are built. Many visitors arrive believing that a small fault means the whole item must be replaced, and the first surprise is often how quickly a loose wire or worn belt can be found. A retired electrical worker who volunteers at the club says that the most useful tool is not a machine but a question: what changed just before the object stopped working? That question turns repair into a form of investigation and helps owners notice details they had ignored.

One student brought a desk lamp that had been left on a shelf for two years, and after replacing a cheap switch she began repairing bike lights for friends. The club also keeps a simple record of failed repairs, because some products are glued shut or use parts that may not be bought separately. These failures are displayed beside successful repairs, not hidden, so visitors can see that not every object can be saved and that design choices affect how long a product lasts. The student and the failed repair shelf show that learning comes from testing, observing, and admitting limits.

Local shops have responded in different ways: some donate spare parts, while others worry that free repairs reduce their income. The organisers reply that the club mainly handles simple faults and often sends complex jobs to professionals, so cooperation can replace doubt. After two years, the group estimates that it has kept more than eight hundred bags of material out of waste. More importantly, visitors leave with a changed habit: they are less likely to throw something away before asking whether it can be understood, opened, and repaired.

questions.stem: What question does the retired electrical worker consider most useful?
options: Which shop sells the strongest new machines.

A library in the north of England lends drills, sewing machines, camping equipment and a set of cake tins, and it has done so since 2015, when a librarian noticed that the most requested item in the catalogue was a power washer that nobody in the town owned.

The logic is simple. (1) ______ A drill is used for eleven minutes in its life, on average, and those eleven minutes cost eighty pounds, so a library that lends one for four pounds a week is doing arithmetic that a shop cannot.

The library's own figures suggest the arithmetic works. Two thousand items sit on the shelves, four hundred are out at any moment, and the subscription pays for a repair bench, two part-time staff and a van that collects donations from garages and attics. The van itself was given by a builder who had retired, and the repair bench is the work of a volunteer who comes in on Thursdays. (2) ______

What has proved harder than the arithmetic is the insurance. A library that lends a ladder is a library that is liable for a fall, and the first policy it could buy excluded anything with a blade, a motor or a ladder. (3) ______ Members now sign a form that names the item, the date and the risk, and the library has not yet had a claim.

The staff are careful with the word community, which they use rarely and precisely. What they report instead is a pattern of borrowing the catalogue did not predict: the same forty households borrow the same six items in rotation, and the library has stopped trying to widen that circle. (4) ______

The librarian who began it is now semi-retired and says the thing she did not expect was the arguments. A member who borrows a drill for a year and a member who borrows one for an hour both regard the library as theirs, and the rules that keep both content are longer than any set she has written before. (5) ______

passages.passage:
Most people believe they are honest with their friends. (1) ______ In practice the opposite is more often true: we stay silent about the habits that damage the people we care about, and call that politeness.

Researchers who study difficult conversations report a pattern. When people are asked to name a piece of feedback they regret not giving, they rarely mention facts. (2) ______ What they describe is a feeling that they let a friendship drift.

One survey of two hundred adults found the same thing: the feedback people most regretted withholding concerned small, repeated behaviour rather than dramatic incidents.

The advice that follows is not to be brutally honest. Brutal honesty usually serves the speaker's relief rather than the listener's benefit. (3) ______ A useful rule is to describe one specific occasion instead of a general tendency, because a tendency sounds like a verdict on a person while an occasion sounds like an event that can be discussed.

Timing matters more than most people expect. A criticism delivered in front of others forces the listener to defend a reputation; the same words delivered a day later, alone, can be considered. (4) ______ That is why many counsellors suggest waiting until both people are calm, even when the wait feels cowardly. Waiting, done properly, is not avoidance; it is choosing a moment when the other person can actually hear you rather than merely endure you.

Finally, it helps to say what you want to happen. Feedback without a request leaves the listener with a problem and no direction. (5) ______ A friend who is told that he always cancels at the last minute learns shame; a friend who is told to send a message by noon if he needs to cancel learns a procedure.

None of this makes the conversation easy. It makes it possible, which is a different and more useful thing. A friendship that survives one honest sentence is usually stronger than one that was protected from every uncomfortable truth.

For example, a manager may rehearse a difficult sentence for weeks.
In short, honesty is always the kindest policy.

passages.passage:
Tourism has an awkward arithmetic: the more people who visit a place, the less there is left of the thing they came to see. (1) ______

The usual remedy is to spread the visitors out, advertising a second valley, a quieter month, a different route. (2) ______ Within five years the second valley has a car park and the quiet month has a queue. The remedy moves the problem instead of solving it, and it moves it to somewhere with fewer defences, where the road is narrow and the water is scarce.

Slower travel is offered as another answer. Instead of four cities in ten days, one town for a week; instead of a photograph at every landmark, an afternoon in a laundry. (3) ______ A guest who stays seven nights buys bread, takes a bus, and notices which shop closes at noon, so that the money arrives in smaller amounts and stays longer.

Critics reply that slowness is a luxury. A week in one place costs more than a week in five, because beds are priced per night and trains per mile. (4) ______ A fishing town that tried the slower version for three summers found that its guest houses earned less per visitor yet kept earning through the winter, which the coach parties never did. The town has since stopped printing its visitor numbers on the harbour wall, preferring a sentence about the number of nights sold.

Governments have begun to accept this arithmetic, at least in public. A regional tourist office now measures the length of stay rather than the number of arrivals, and a mayor who once printed arrival figures on the front of a brochure talks instead about how many nights the town can absorb before its water supply fails.

The argument is not really about speed. It is about who pays for the place being worth visiting. (5) ______ A town that can afford to stay ordinary will still be worth the journey in twenty years.
